articleTitle: Intergation of Interdigitated Electrodes to Quantum Dot Based Photoconductive Antenna Unconventionally Enhances Pulsed Terahertz Generation
abstract: We investigate the quantum dot based photoconductive antennas with interdigated and conventional electrodes for pulsed THz generation. We report that the photoconductive antennas with interdigitated electrodes shows an unconventional enhancement of pulsed terahertz radiation by up to 3 times the conventional photoconductive antennas.

articleTitle: Tunable low-loss silicon nitride integrated circuits
abstract: We present tunable photonic integrated circuits platform with low losses in a wide wavelength bandwidth from 900 to 1550 nm based on Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> waveguides.

articleTitle: Distributed Acoustic Sensing over 146 km using Phase-sensitive Optical Time-domain Reflectometer assisted by bidirectional distributed Raman amplifier
abstract: We demonstrate the operation of a distributed acoustic sensor (DAS) based on a phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varphi \text{OTDR})$</tex> assisted by a bidirectional distributed Raman amplifier over a distance of 146 km without blind zones.

articleTitle: A Neural Network Method For The BFS Extraction
abstract: We present a method for increasing the accuracy of determining the Brillouin frequency shift in a fiber strain sensor. A neural network which using the results obtained from other methods as input data and the parameters of the system is applied. The result is an additional 10% accuracy increasing, which is significant given that existing methods have already reached their limit and work at low SNR values (about 5 dB).

articleTitle: Compensation of Wavelength Instability in $\Phi$-OTDR with Weak Fiber Bragg Gratings
abstract: We propose a scheme of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex>-OTDR, which includes irregularly arranged weak fiber Bragg gratings (wFBG) in sensing fiber for laser wavelength instability measurement and compensation. In a scheme with 4 pairs of wFBG, wavelength shift is measured with 16 times higher resolution, which allows reducing the effect of laser instability on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex>-OTDR accuracy.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Distributed Acoustic Sensor Based on Sagnac Interferometer
abstract: We report on a study of sensitivity distribution over the loop of a Sagnac interferometer, which is one of the most important characteristics of distributed acoustic sensors, applied for long perimeters, pipelines, and railways security and monitoring. In result of numerical simulation we demonstrate that sensitivity has harmonic dependence on position and frequency of the disturbance.

articleTitle: Compact transportable CH4 PAD gas analyzer based on quantum cascade laser
abstract: Compact transportable CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> photoacoustic gas analyzer based on PAD detector and quantum cascade laser at 7.65 μm was created.

articleTitle: Acousto-optic two-dimensional modulators based on monoclinic KYW crystal
abstract: Symmetries of acousto-optic interaction in mono-clinic crystals enable design of two-coordinate modulators and deflectors. We designed and fabricated a series of acousto-optic devices based on potassium yttrium tungstate crystal, KY(WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)2. The prototypes of monolithic acousto-optic modulators are capa-ble of two-coordinate deflection of unpolarized laser beams and controlling output polarization.

articleTitle: Helicobacter pylori breath test by the Raman spectroscopy gas analyzer
abstract: The features of the Helicobacter pylori pathogen diagnosis in the human gastrointestinal tract using Raman spectroscopy are described. The estimation of the Raman gas analyzer resolution was conducted. Experimental measurement of a gas mixture with a known composition has been carried out.

articleTitle: Phosphorescent Ir(III) oxygen sensors for bioimaging
abstract: This work is devoted to the design, synthesis and implementation of novel iridium(III) O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensors in bioimaging.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of an ultrafast Tm-doped fibre laser with third-order dispersion compensation
abstract: Tm-doped fibre laser with intracavity third-order dispersion compensation is developed. The numerically simulated pulses have a smooth symmetrical shape and following characteristics: time FWHM of 2 ps, spectral FWHM of 28 nm, 50 MHz repetition rate, average power of 2.5 mW, pulse energy of 48 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$pJ$</tex>.

articleTitle: Functions for Describing Nonexponential Photoluminescence Decay Kinetics in Semiconductor Nanocrystals
abstract: We briefly review functions that we have proposed for the description of the experimentally observed nonexponential photoluminescence (PL) decay kinetics of colloidal quantum dots (QDs) at room temperature (RT) with parameters that have a straightforward physical meaning.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Resistance to Ionizing Radiation of Optical Products Based on the AgBr - AgI System Crystals
abstract: The photo- and radiation resistance of optical windows and fibers based on the AgBr-AgI system crystals has been studied. The greatest optical loss during irradiation with ultraviolet for 530 min does not exceed 40% in the entire transmission range. The transmission spectra show the resistance of fibers to electron irradiation with doses up to 400 kGy.

articleTitle: Laser Damage Attack on a Simple Optical Attenuator Widely Used in Fiber-based QKD Systems
abstract: We present the results of an experimental study of laser damage attack (LDA) from the CW laser power up to 5.5 W at a wavelength of 1561 at a simple type of commercially available attenuator widely used in telecommunications and fiber-based QKD systems.

articleTitle: Growth, Thermal Conductivity and Spectroscopic properties of Nd:MgMoO4 Laser Crystal
abstract: The series of Neodymium-doped magnesium molybdate crystals (Nd:MgMoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) belonging to the monoclinic class (sp. gr. C2/m) was grown by the Czochralski method from the charges underwent the special physical treatments. Complex of polarized optical spectroscopic studies was performed. The actual Nd concentrations in the crystals, as well as the unit cell parameters were measured. The peculiarities of the crystals growth process and of the measured properties in connection with the kind of the special charge treatment are discussed.

articleTitle: The Effect of Optical Losses on the CW Oxygen-Iodine Laser Power Efficiency
abstract: The cw oxygen-iodine lasers operating modes mapping method has been modified. This makes it possible, with known kinetic and optical losses, to determine the dimensional parameters corresponding to regimes with high power efficiency.

articleTitle: Development of laser method for studying temperature distribution in active elements of high average power laser amplifiers
abstract: This work is devoted to the method for studying temperature distribution in solid-state active elements of high average power laser amplifiers. Temperature distribution in an active element of the cryogenically-cooled diode-pumped laser amplifier with high average power were investigated and analyzed. The investigation was carried out for various pump beam diameters and repetition rates 500 and 1000 Hz.

articleTitle: Laser-induced optical chirality in planar plasmonic nanostructures
abstract: Demonstration of optical chirality in plasmon nanostructures made of silver on a dielectric substrate prepared by subsequent annealing and laser treatments was shown for the first time.

articleTitle: Development of laser elements with non-linear distribution of active ions
abstract: An approach associated with the use of active media with a non-uniform dopant ions concentration distribution is proposed to increase the pulse energy level and optimize the high power laser amplifier parameters. The optimal profiles of the laser-active ions gradient distribution in the amplifying medium were determined. A crystal sample was obtained in which the concentration of the activator changes sharply from 5 at.% to 10 at.% over a length of 3–5 mm.

articleTitle: Finding the Route of Laying the Optical Cable Using the Coherent Reflectometer
abstract: A technique for searching for a damaged optical cable using the optical coherent reflectometer and vibration action has been developed and tested under the conditions of an operating facility

articleTitle: Detection of Influenza A and B viruses by Raman spectroscopy
abstract: As Raman spectroscopy allows the study of organic compounds' structure and composition in aqueous solutions, it is often chosen as a tool for detecting and identifying viruses in human biological fluids, such as saliva and pharyngeal secretions, urine, and blood. Our work demonstrates that the Raman scattering signal combined with machine learning algorithms can be used as an express method for diagnosing viral diseases.

articleTitle: Laser mass spectrometry of volatile organic compounds for diagnostics of kidney damage
abstract: A method of laser mass spectrometric express analysis of volatile organic compounds (VOC) without sample preparation is proposed. VUV radiation of laser plasma is used for VOCs ionization. The method was applied for early diagnostics of kidney damage in children with congenital uropathy.

articleTitle: Concentration Quenching of the Fe2+ Luminescence in a ZnSe Single Crystal
abstract: It is measured the kinetics of the luminescence of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ in ZnSe at liquid nitrogen temperature at excitation by short laser pulse with wavelength 2940 nm. It was showed that the form of luminescence decay curve depends on concentration of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>. This was interpreted as a manifestation of concentration quenching of upper state of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>.

articleTitle: Optical loss and noise modelling in microdisk lasers with InGaAs quantum well-dots
abstract: Optical loss of different origin was quantitatively evaluated in micrlaser disk resonators. Active region represents InGaAs quantum dots of very high surface density. We found that surface absorption predominantly determines the optical loss in these microresonators, and the scattering loss is responsible for the slope efficiency. The small-signal modulation characteristics of microdisk lasers bonded onto a silicon substrate by thermocompression method were studied. The suppression of the side modes reaches 27 dB already at 1.7xthreshold. The relative optical intensity noise was simulated as a function of the bias current. It is shown that the integral noise is low enough for error-free optical data transmission with the maximum possible bitrate limited by the modulation bandwidth.

articleTitle: Bessel beam generation from conically refracted laser diode radiation
abstract: We demonstrate generation of Bessel beam from conically refracted laser diode radiation. Conical refraction provides annular distribution of the beam at the axicon that is favorable for efficient Bessel beam generation.

articleTitle: Synthesis of luminescent hybrid materials in the PbF2-La(Y)F3- (8-hydroxyquinolate) lithium system by co-precipitation technique
abstract: Organic-inorganic luminescent hybrid materials with an inorganic matrix based on mixed lead and rare-earth fluorides and (8-hydroxyquinolate) lithium as an organic phosphor by co-precipitation from aqueous solutions have been synthesized. Their phase compositions and spectral characteristics have been investigated. The synthesized hybrid materials showed efficient broadband photoluminescence in the 390–700 nm region.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: Setup for Acoustic Sensitivity Measurements of Fiber Optic Cables Based on Weak FBGs
abstract: We report on a study of a new scheme for acoustic sensitivity measurements of fiber optic cables. It uses a Fizeau interferometer scheme with weak fiber Bragg gratings as a mirrors. It's advantage is the absence of interferometer reference arm which exclude noise influence on it and on other parts of scheme.

articleTitle: The influence of Sc3+ ions on fluorescence lifetime of Yb3+ in Yb- doped yttrium scandium aluminum garnet (Yb:YSAG) ceramics
abstract: We present the luminescence radiative lifetime data of Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> in Yb- doped yttrium scandium aluminum garnet (Yb:YSAG) ceramics at room temperature (300 K). The results show that the Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> lifetime changes significantly with content of Sc<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ion in Yb:YSAG and depends on the crystallography position occupied by Sc<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>. The ceramics with the highest Sc<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> content in octahedral position has longer luminescence radiative lifetimes.

articleTitle: Using Disk-Detector Geometry for Calculation of Optical Path Length by Monte Carlo Simulation of Light Transport in Turbid Media
abstract: Disk-detector geometry replacing a conventional square detector with a disk detector is a technique designed to speed up Monte Carlo simulations of light transport in turbid media, such as tissues, in the context of a backscattering problem. In this study, applicability of using this technique to calculate optical path length traveled by photons in a medium is tested. It is shown that such calculations are performed correctly and their accuracy is higher than in the case of square detectors.

articleTitle: Comparison of Methods for Calculating Thermal Frequency Shifts in Integrated Si3N4 Microresonators
abstract: Heating is inevitable effect in crystaline and inte-grated whispering gallery mode microresonators, as they usually accumulate high power inside. In this work different methods of thermomechanical processes modeling in such systems are studied. We show that the commonly used simplified model can be inconsistent with direct numerical approach.

articleTitle: New time-domain spectroscopic methods at Novosibirsk FEL
abstract: Powerful coherent pulse-periodical radiation of the terahertz Novosibirsk free-electron laser (NovoFEL) allows to carry out unique experiments in the field of time-domain spectroscopy. Different spectroscopic methods from ultrafast (measuring time - 200 ps, resolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-2\cdot 10^{-3}$</tex>) to super-high unlimited resolution are presented in the report.

articleTitle: The effect of laser frequency drift on the response of Phase-sensitive Optical Time-domain Reflectometer
abstract: We present numerical simulations of the Dual-pulse Phase-sensitive Optical Time-domain Reflectometer which response is affected by the laser optical frequency drift. The phase signals retrieved from fixed fiber positions (channels) demonstrate random jumps. Corresponding phase noise spectra approximated by a combination of white noise determined by the laser linewidth and flicker phase noise determined by the laser optical frequency drift rate.

articleTitle: Perovskite-polymer nanocomposites based on nanofibers for flexible solar cells
abstract: We study the crystallinity and light absorption properties of CsPbI3: polyvinylpyrrolidone nanofibers, which can be used as active layers for solar cells. Experimental results show that the black phase of CsPbI3 nanocrystals can be manipulated using the annealing parameters.

articleTitle: Using the SERS method and machine learning technology to detect the influenza A virus
abstract: The worldwide pandemic caused by Covid-19 demonstrates the need to develop new methods for the respiratory viral diseases' diagnosis, which should be fast and accurate. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) can be one of such methods. Our work demonstrated the possibility of using SERS technology and machine learning for fast (about 30 seconds) and accurate detection of the influenza A virus in a biological sample.

articleTitle: Intraoperative video-fluorescence navigation by PpIX and tissue saturation measurement during surgical resection of gastric malignant tumor
abstract: Fluorescence visualization of pathologies is a popular form of endoscopic diagnostics in medicine. Interest in fluorescence optical visualization consists in providing information on the fluorescent signal spatial distribution by the photosensitizer fluorescence, which has a selective accumulation in tumor. Together with this, the determination of tissue saturation makes possible to assess the adequate of blood supply to anastomosis during surgical operation.

articleTitle: The excitation modes of porous silicon microcavities with an embedded conjugated polymer for detecting vapors of nitroaromatic compounds
abstract: Currently, fluorescent sensors for detection of explosives are being actively developed. One of the important issues, along with the sensitivity and speed of analysis, is the stability of the fluorescence of a sensitive luminophore, and the natural degradation of its fluorescence under the action of exciting radiation. In this work, we study the fluorescence response of MDMO-PPV embedded in a porous silicon microcavity to trinitrotoluene vapors under the action of exciting radiation with different intensities and wavelength of 450 nm. The conclusion is made about the preferred mode of the luminophore excitation.

articleTitle: Two-stage method for comparing the lengths of optical fibers using OFDR
abstract: The paper proposes a two-stage method for comparing the lengths of optical fibers using the optical frequency domain reflectometry. The method was applied for comparing of of two fibers lengths.

Author Keywords: measurement of the length of the fiber

articleTitle: Accounting for microbends in determining induced birefringence in a ring fiber-optic resonator
abstract: It is proposed to take into account the microbends of an optical fiber in order to find the induced birefringence in a ring resonator. It is shown that, due to the small bending radius at the coupling regions, the contribution from these regions to the total change in the optical length is comparable with the contribution of the main part of the resonator contour.

articleTitle: Superconducting Single-photon detector design optimization
abstract: A new SNSPD topology is proposed, in which, according to the simulation results, the least current crowding effect is observed, which makes it the most preferable for the creation of an SNSPD with a high quantum efficiency and a low dark count rate.

articleTitle: The concept of a pulsed neuromorphic optical system based on a 3D model of an optical neuron
abstract: A 3D-model of an artificial optical neuron is proposed for scalable implementation of pulsed neuromorphic optical system.

articleTitle: The State Primary Standard of the Unit of Length - the meter GET 2
abstract: The report is about the The State Primary Standard of the Unit of Length - the meter GET 2.

articleTitle: Multicore Fibers with Interacting Cores for Coherently Combined High-Power Laser Systems
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally and numerically that in the multicore fiber with a square array of cores the out-of-phase supermode, which is stable at high power, can steadily propagate and can be coherently combined at the output with high efficiency. In numerical modeling 70 MW peak power can be achieved by using tapered active multicore fiber with an 11×11 array of cores.

articleTitle: Spectral properties of CsPbI3 perovskite nanocrystals in borogermanate glass
abstract: The investigation results of spectral properties of CsPbI3 perovskite nanocrystals in borogermanate glass are presented. The nanocrystals luminescence band shifts from 670 to 710 nm with crystal size increase from 6.3 to 17 nm. The maximum quantum yield obtained is 34%.

articleTitle: Laser amplification in active elements with high temperature gradient
abstract: A time-dependent model of laser amplification in an Yb:YAG crystal is developed, with accounting of active media thermophysical and laser characteristics dependencies on the temperature distribution, the dependence of the gain medium laser characteristics on the seed wavelength and the effect of amplified spontaneous emission. The numerical simulation of the laser amplification process in the active element of a multidisk amplifier was performed and compared to experimental results.

articleTitle: Gas Tubine Vibration Monitoring via Fiber Optic Sensor
abstract: We report on a study of vibration measurements of a gas turbine via fiber optic sensor based on a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The experiment allows controlling the rotation frequency and detecting acoustic signals from some defects in construction. Phase unwrapping scheme of fiber interferometer and spectrogram analysis provide the measurement information.

articleTitle: High-speed video recording of liquid melt spraying during ablation of the Y2O3 target using a fiber ytterbium laser
abstract: A Highspeed video shooting of liquid melt splashing during the ablation of Nd:Y203 target with the ytterbium fiber laser was made. Using the CuBr laser monitor for shooting allowed to eliminate bright laser plasma luminescence on pictures and to see splashing of drops right from the target crater. The splashing of liquid melt is a difficult hydrodynamic process. Usually the melt splashes out in separate jets, splitting into droplets already in the air, but sometimes single droplets form immediately.

articleTitle: Wavelength tuned mid-IR lasers based on single-crystalline or polycrystalline Cr2+-doped ZnSe with $1.9-2.1\ \mu\mathrm{m}$ pumping
abstract: Poly- and single-crystalline Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>:ZnSe pumped by the repetitively-pulsed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.1\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> Ho<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>: YAG laser or CW fiber laser at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.91\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> were used as the laser active elements. An acousto-optically filters were used for the wavelength tuning of the laser wavelength within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.3-2.7\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>. The power scaling in the master oscillator - power amplifier laser systems of the wavelength-tuned Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>: ZnSe output is discussed.

articleTitle: An ex vivo study of the impact of mid-infrared laser on ocular tissues
abstract: We are searching for the most suitable laser radiation, which will allow us to make thin cuts on the retina and choroid with high accuracy, minimal damage to surrounding tissues, and a sufficient degree of coagulation to prevent hemorrhages. As the first wavelength at which we conducted research, we chose 3.0 µm. This is primarily due to the fact that this wavelength coincides with the peak of the spectral absorption of water. The retina, choroid and sclera of pig eyes were used as biological tissue. The impact of laser radiation on eye tissues was assessed using a scanning electron microscope. According to the results of the experiment, laser radiation with a given wavelength has a deep penetration of radiation into the sclera up to 300 µm, with a crater width of 250–480 microns. Collateral damage in the sclera is less than 80 microns. When exposed to laser radiation on the choroid: the penetration depth was up to 150 µm, the width of the crater was up to 110 µm, collateral damage was up to 70 µm. The retina, when exposed to radiation with the specified settings, is cut through. The higher the energy and frequency of radiation, the deeper its penetration, wider cut and collateral damage to biological tissue.

articleTitle: Investigation of obtaining ZnSe nanopowders by means of a fiber ytterbium laser
abstract: The production of zinc selenide nanopowder using repetitively pulsed radiation from a ytterbium fiber laser has been studied. With an average radiation power of 300 W and a pulse duration of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$120\ \mu\mathrm{s}$</tex>, the productivity of nanopowder production was ≈100 g/h. The nanopowder contains weakly agglomerated particles that have a spherical shape, as well as the shape of polyhedrons. Their arithmetic average size is 18 nm. Nanoparticles have two crystalline phases: cubic (40 wt.%), and hexagonal (60 wt. %).

Author Keywords: gas-p IPG Photonics hase method for obtaining nanoparticles

articleTitle: Designing Mamyshev oscillator cavity by particle swarm optimization algorithm
abstract: We apply particle swarm algorithm for numerical optimization of a Mamyshev oscillator. We demonstrate that our approach can be used for design of laser configuration with megawatt peak power scale.

articleTitle: Ghost imaging based on broadband terahertz radiation
abstract: Speckle structures formed by the propagation of broadband pulsed terahertz radiation through the transparent plate with random phase inhomogeneity were numerically and experimentally confirmed. The possibility of utilizing formed speckle structures and reduction of required measurements due to spectral multiplexing for the implementation of the ghost imaging technique has been demonstrated by the methods of numerical modeling.

articleTitle: Application of wearable multimodal devices to study microcirculatory-tissue systems under microgravity conditions
abstract: This paper presents the first results of the study of changes in microcirculatory-tissue systems functioning under spaceflight conditions.

articleTitle: Planar CO- and CO2-lasers with an unstable cavity and additional feedback
abstract: The radiation of planar RF-excited CO- and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-lasers with an unstable resonator and one coupling element is spatially superimposed. The divergence and emission spectrum are investigated. It is shown that in CO- and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-lasers it is possible, by acting on the peripheral part of the composite resonator, to increase the output power and lower the lasing threshold.

Author Keywords: Carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide lasers

articleTitle: Ultracompact fluorescence LIDAR for drone based autonomous monitoring in agriculture
abstract: We have developed the ultracompact (~300 g) fluorescence LIDAR and installed it on a quadrocopter for remote sensing of vegetation. LIDAR was based on diode laser (405 nm, 150 m W) and mini-spectrometer but the instrument can acquire fluorescence spectra from a 8 m distance. LIDAR was utilized for remote mapping of maize field during different periods of maize growth to indicate healthy and diseased maize plants. The field tests have proved utilization of autonomous LIDAR monitoring for early crop disease detection.

articleTitle: Bifurcation Bridges In Mode-Locked Frequency-Swept Feedback Lasers
abstract: We describe and explain the periodic mode-locked regime and its mechanisms of occurrence in a frequency swept SG-DBR laser source with continuous optical feedback. We propose that mode-locked operation results from the resonant perturbation of bridges of periodic solutions existing in a non-swept system with feedback.

articleTitle: Waveguiding via Transformation Optics
abstract: We demonstrate that it is possible to surpass current limitations of nanophotonics and plasmonics by designing an artificial material which can emulate user-defined spatial refractive index distribution. The effective optical property of the material is engineered through the deformation of reflective substrate via transformation optics approach. We provide one of possible applications - subwavelength optical waveguide coupler device based on this technique.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of NLC Director Deformation Using a Combination of Aberration Self-Action and Polarization Microscopy Methods
abstract: The processes of light-induced orientation at oblique incidence of a light beam on a dye-doped nematic liquid crystal (NLC) are experimentally studied with the simultaneous use of the methods of aberrational light beam self-action and polarization microscopy. Each method has features associated with the geometry of light propagation in an NLC, and their combination significantly expands the possibilities of reconstructing the light-induced profile of the nonlinear phase shift and director deformation field.

articleTitle: Far field dynamics of strongly coupled narrow stripe ridge-waveguide laser arrays (1060 nm)
abstract: The temporal behavior of an optical power at different moments of pulse in the far field is studied for a laser array <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda=1060\ \text{nm})$</tex> based on InGaAs/AlGaAs/GaAs. An array of narrow-stripe laser diodes with a straight ridge of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.5-\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> width and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$13.5\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> -wide pitch without distributed feedback elements demonstrates that despite the strong optical coupling between adjacent array elements the lateral far fields only slightly differ from each other in width at half maximum (FWHM) (by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.5^{\circ}$</tex>) at different moments of the pulse (130 ns/1 kHz) at a pump current amplitude of 5 A.

articleTitle: Investigation of the divergence and spectral characteristics of radiation from a planar cw laser with an unstable resonator and additional feedback
abstract: The problems of divergence and spectral selection of RF excited planar CO- and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-lasers radiation are considered. These lasers with an unstable optical cavity had an additional external mirror (translucent plate with a transmission of 67 and 85%, respectively) located outside the laser model.

Author Keywords: planar carbon monoxide and dioxide lasers

articleTitle: Phase space investigation of electron acceleration in direct laser acceleration (DLA)
abstract: Developed simplified analytically solvable model of DLA, supported by the numerical integration of equation of motion, demonstrates the possibility of ionization injection into the plasma channel at a rather wide range of its parameters and initial phases.

articleTitle: Study of Hemo- and Lympho-Dynamics in the Healing Process of Laser Wound on Mouse Skin
abstract: This work presents a study of hemo- and limpho-microcirculation in mouse skin before and after exposure to laser radiation, as well as studying changes in microcirculation in the healing process of the wound using laser Doppler flowmetry. The continuous-wave (CW) radiation was induced using an all-fiber holmium (Ho) laser with a wavelength of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.1\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Parallel-gap resistance microwelding for deformable mirror manufacturing
abstract: Creation of reliable electrical connection on piezoceramic disk in bimorph deformable mirror is very important and challenging task, especially for small-aperture piezoelectric wavefront correctors. We propose to use parallel-gap resistance microwelding as an effective tool to achieve a good quality of bonding between wire and piezodisk surface and to increase tensile strength of contact in the Ag-Cu (silver-copper) system.

articleTitle: Synthesis of polymer-coated metal-organic frameworks for gene delivery
abstract: Gene therapy is on the cutting edge of modern medicine, thus delivery of gene of interest (GOI) is an ongoing challenging task. Here, we performed optimization of synthesis of polymer-coated metal-organic frameworks with magnetic core, aiming to improve their ability to be nucleic acid carriers. We varied different synthesis parameters to investigate their impact on DNA-binding capacity as well as on the ability of certain nanoparticles to be a vehicle for in vitro transfection.

Author Keywords: GOI delivery in vitro and in vivo

articleTitle: Physical background of Nd3+, Yb3+: YF3 temperature sensors for biomedical applications
abstract: The studied N d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+, Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+: YF3 nanoparticles demonstrated high (0.01 K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) temperature sensitivity in the physiological temperature range. The mechanism of temperature sensitivity includes phonon-assisted energy transfer processes between doping ions, as well as lattice distortion due to thermal expansion phenomenon.

Author Keywords: temperature sensitivity in the physiological range

articleTitle: Fluorescence Anisotropy of FAD in Water-Propylene Glycol Solutions under Excitation by Picosecond Laser Pulses at 355 nm
abstract: The experimental study of fluorescence anisotropy decay of FAD in water-propylene glycole solutions under excitation by picosecond laser pulses at 355 nm was carried out. Initial anisotropies and rotational diffusion times were determined from experimental data by fit. The determined relationship between the rotational diffusion times and solvent viscosity was compared with that in water-methanol solutions.

articleTitle: Variable Envelope Shape and Width Hybrid Pulse-Burst Laser Source
abstract: The simple hybrid laser pulse-burst source is presented. The ability to manage pulse burst envelope shape and width was demonstrated. Intra-burst pulses duration and energies were 20 ps and 1.5 mJ, respectively.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulations of the Electromagnetic Fields' Distribution in Dielectric Microspheres With High Size Parameter
abstract: The near-field electromagnetic distribution arising from the light scattering of a large dielectric microsphere is discussed in the framework of the Mie theory. Particular attention is devoted to the formation of photonic nanojets. We aim to characterize the conditions to exploit the microsphere as probes for surface-sensitive spectroscopy and imaging applications.

articleTitle: Dynamics of a laser diode self-injection locked to a whispering gallery mode microresonator
abstract: We have studied a laser diode self-injection locking to the modes of whispering gallery mode microresonator (WGMM) in a wide range of parameters and derived several regularities allowing optimization of the locking process. In this work we investigated in detail the optimization process, based on the thermal nonlinearity of the WGMM modes, when the laser frequency is tuned smoothly to the WGMM frequency (adiabatic tuning).

articleTitle: Strain-estimation-based OCT angiography
abstract: Visualization of microvasculature in Optical Coherence Angiography (OCA) is based on discrimination of erythrocytes' motion against the surrounding “solid” tissue. Most OCA methods use discrimination of temporal speckle variability in OCT images; high speckle variability corresponds to blood vessels. In this study, we present a new principle of OCA based on estimation of local interframe strains. We compare the new method with the high-pass filtering OCA technique that uses temporal speckle variability. In the comparison we use both simulation data and experimental measurements. The new OCA method shows higher tolerance to artifacts induced by strong inhomogeneous strains, which is very promising for realization of contact-mode OCA intended for practical applications on patients.

articleTitle: Angular dispersion boost of high order laser harmonics interacting with dense plasma clusters
abstract: We propose a nanosphere array target in the plasma phase as an efficient dispersive medium for the intense XUV light originated from laser-plasma interactions where various high harmonic generation processes take place. The scattering process is studied with the help of numerical simulations using resonance conditions obtained from the analytical model. We show that the angular distribution of different harmonics after scattering can be good described by a simple interference, in particular for the rectangle symmetry the angular distribution corresponds to the Bragg-Wolfe diffraction theory.

articleTitle: TEA-N2 laser with pulse repetition rate up to 12 kilohertz
abstract: Electrode structures of the “set of points - plane” type with individual excitation of volume discharges in each section from one pulse generator in the presence of preionization ensure the operation of TEA-N2 lasers at pulse repetition frequencies up to 10–12 kHz. A mixture of nitrogen and helium was used as a working medium at a total pressure of 760 Torr. The stabilization of the energy parameters of the radiation pulses for a long time was ensured by the continuous updating of the gas medium in the active element.

articleTitle: Mode-locking in a YAG:Cr4+ solid-state laser gyroscope
abstract: This paper presents a YAG:Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>+ solid-state laser gyroscope in which mode locking is used to improve accuracy. Mode locking makes it possible to reduce the competition of counterpropagating waves and weaken the coupling of counterpropagating waves; in addition, it reduces the spectral width of the longitudinal modes. In this work, studies and analysis of the influence of mode locking on the characteristics of a laser gyroscope, in particular, the accuracy parameters, are carried out.

articleTitle: Dual-lobe Optical Frequency Comb Laser
abstract: We report the observation of a dual lobe optical and RF spectrum in the output of a 8 GHz integrated passively mode-locked laser. We demonstrate the independent tuning of the mode beating frequencies of each lobe by applying a RF modulation of the saturable absorber.

articleTitle: Light Sheet Flow Cytometry: Study of Polyelectrolyte Microcapsules in Whole Blood
abstract: Lightsheet-based flow cytometry system with the ability of measuring in the whole undiluted blood and magnetic separation of objects of interest was developed. It was used to investigate how the magnetic targeting of polyelectrolyte microcapsules influenced by the concentration of magnetic nanoparticles, microcapsule size and flow speed in the vessel.

articleTitle: Temperature dependences of spectral and power characteristics of quantum cascade lasers with frequencies from 2.3 to 4.1 THz
abstract: We conduct research of quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) emitting at 2.3, 3.2 and 4.1 THz. Measuring the output power, we consider the potential mechanisms of QCL temperature degradation. Additionally, we present the spectra of the lasers measured in a wide temperature range 5 -120 K.

articleTitle: Efficient Double-Lyot Spectral Filtering for Mode-Locked Tm-doped all-PM Fiber Laser
abstract: We report on the first demonstration of the mode-locked Tm-doped all-PM fiber laser with two fiber Lyot filters embedded into the ring resonator. This approach allows us to efficiently tune the central wavelength of laser generation to ~ 1855 nm as well as to adjust spectrum width for required pulse duration.

articleTitle: Co:MgAl2O4 Ceramic Saturable Absorbers Fabricated by Pressure Slip Casting and HIPing
abstract: Transparent cobalt-doped spinel ceramics 0.02 – 0.1 at. % Co: MgAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> were fabricated by Hot Isostatic Pressing using green bodies formed by pressure slip casting. Their microstructure, optical and spectroscopic properties were studied. For the 0.02 at.% Co-doped ceramic, the saturation fluence at 1535 nm is 0.36 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the laser induced damage threshold is about 4 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Down-Conversion Luminescence of Yb3+ Ions in Yb:CaWO4 Single Crystals
abstract: Ytterbium and ytterbium -niobium doped sheelite single crystals have been grown by the Czochralski method in air and in protective atmospheres and subjected to additional annealing in air, in CO/CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> atmosphereand in forevacuum. Comparative investigations of optical absorption and photoluminescence spectra of the crystals in the visible and near-IR spectral regions upon UV excitation were performed. A consistent pattern is proposed, explaining the nature of the donor centers involved into the process of down-conversion population of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</inf> excited state of Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ ions in the crystals.

articleTitle: Growth, Structure and Spectroscopy of a Novel Molybdate Laser Crystal - $\text{Tm}:\text{MgMoO}_{4}$
abstract: Thulium-doped magnesium molybdate crystal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Tm: \text{MgMoO}_{4})$</tex> was grown by the Czochralski method. It belongs to the monoclinic class (sp. gr. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C2/m)$</tex>. Its spectroscopic properties are studied. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Tm}:\text{MgMoO}_{4}$</tex> exhibits broad and smooth emission spectrum extending beyond <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\ \mu\mathrm{m}({{}^{3}\mathrm{F}}_{4}\rightarrow {{}^{3}\mathrm{H}}_{6}$</tex> transition) and a long lifetime of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{}^{3}\mathrm{F}}_{4}$</tex> state (1.90 ms) making it promising for broadly tunable and mode-locked lasers.

articleTitle: Morphological and functional assessment of tumorand non-tumor tissue under therapy using multimodalOCT
abstract: The aim of this study is compare the early (within 24 hours) blood vessels reaction to photodynamic therapy (PDT) by optical coherence angiography (OCA) in case of tumor (basal cell carcinoma) and inflammation lesions (vulvar lichen sclerosus). It was shown that the microvascular damages was the primary reaction to PDT whereas tumor cells necrosis was the secondary response. The blood vessels reaction and its dynamic was universal for both tumor and inflammation lesions.

articleTitle: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering from 1D-3D plasmonic Au nanoparticles: the fourth-power law revisited
abstract: According to theoretical estimates, the SERS signal is proportional to the fourth power of the local field, so the maximum intensity should strongly depend on the tuning of the plasmon resonance to the excitation wavelength. However, the experimental data, which are very few, do not confirm the fourth-power law. In this work, the dependence of the SERS enhancement factor on the plasmon resonance tuning for 1D-3D plasmonic nanoparticles is studied for the first time using the gold nanorod, nanotriangle, and nanostar samples obtained by controlled etching and functionalized with Raman molecules. The measured enhancement factors are compared with simulations based on COMSOL and T-matrix method.

articleTitle: Multilayer Volumetric Modification of Fused Silica by Femtosecond Laser Radiation
abstract: We demonstrate the possibility of multilayer information writing in the volume of transparent media by femtosecond laser. The results of multilayer ordered structures formation in the bulk of the transparent fused silica glass samples are demonstrated. Examples of modification of a refractive index by means of interaction ultrashort laser pulses are shown.

articleTitle: BaMgF4 whispering-gallery-mode crystal resonator with high Q-factor
abstract: Optical whispering gallery mode (WGM) microres-onators can combine small mode volume, high-power density, and large Q-factor. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}\boldsymbol{a}\boldsymbol{M}\boldsymbol{g}\boldsymbol{F}_{4}$</tex> is an advanced material for modern photonics that exhibits an ultra-wide transparency range. Unfortunately, there were no reports on manufacturing a high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q\ \boldsymbol{B}\boldsymbol{a}\boldsymbol{M}\boldsymbol{g}\boldsymbol{F}_{4}$</tex> microresonator until now. For the first time, we report on a Q-factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.2\times 10^{7}$</tex> in crystalline z-cut <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}\boldsymbol{a}\boldsymbol{M}\boldsymbol{g}\boldsymbol{F}_{4}$</tex> optical microresonators at 1550 nm wavelength.

articleTitle: Low-cost magnetic Fe alloy based THz polarization filters in EVA matrix
abstract: We present the dependence of the concentration of magnetic driven 5BDSR alloy of THz filters in EVA matrix, on absorption and reflection properties in the extended THz range of 0.2-2 THz. Transmittance dependence on particles concentration and orientation was studied using a custom-made THz-TDS spectrometer. The extinction coefficient of up to 20 was obtained using 15 mass.% of 5BDSR alloy.

articleTitle: Turbulent state switching in mode-locked fiber lasers
abstract: Our simulations demonstrate the switching of stable mode-locking, turbulent, and laminar in a nonlinear polarization rotation mode-locked fiber laser by tuning the polarization controller, which advances the understanding of turbulence in the framework of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation.

articleTitle: Role of kinetics in spontaneous segregation of group III elements in arsenide nanowires
abstract: A model of spontaneous formation of the radial heterostructure in arsenide nanowire in single process is proposed. Good agreement of theory and experiment was demonstrated for (In,As)As nanowires. This could be considered as an alternative approach to formation of core-shell heterostructure.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Parasitic Effects in a Ring Confocal Resonator when Operating as A Gyroscope Sensing Element
abstract: The paper analyzes and evaluates the parasitic effects that can manifest in a ring confocal resonator when it operates as a sensitive element of an optical resonator gyroscope.

articleTitle: Stress-Strained State of Brittle Materials after Picosecond Laser Treatment in Package High-Frequency Pulsation Mode
abstract: The mathematical model is proposed that describes the physical picture of mechanical processes occurring in solid brittle materials when exposed to picosecond pulsed laser radiation. A package mode of laser equipment operation is considered, when packets of several picosecond pulses follow with a lag of each other by a time of the nanoseconds order (high-frequency pulsation mode). In this mode removal of matter from the treated surface, provoked by the “Coulomb explosion” (cold ablation), generates a pulsed reactive force. This force creates a high-pressure region in the laser-matter interaction zone. This can cause the appearance of plastic deformations in metals or the destruction of brittle materials both inside this area and outside it. In order to minimize the negative effect of the processing mode and to get closed as possible to non-destructive action, an analytical tool has been developed for the deliberate choice of parameters of laser action on brittle and pseudo-brittle materials. In the proposed model, the study of the stress-strained state of the plate is reduced to determining the deflection of its median plane by solving the dynamic problem of the theory of elasticity. The paper shows the application of the developed model to the calculation of the modes of laser processing of glass-carbon and molybdenum when creating micropoint structures.

articleTitle: Modeling the formation of self-catalyzed GaAs and GaP nanowires
abstract: We present a theoretical model to depict the formation of self-catalyzed GaAs and GaP nanowires. The growth regimes of monolayer on the nanowire top facet are investigated.

articleTitle: Anisotropic relaxation of Radachlorin photosensitizer in aqueous solution under two-photon excitation
abstract: The fluorescence decay of Radachlorin photosensitizer in aqueous solution under two-photon excitation by femtosecond laser pulses at 810 nm has been studied. The major fluorescence parameters of the molecule including fluorescence decay time, rotational diffusion time and anisotropy have been determined.

articleTitle: Mid-infrared Emission Properties of Transparent Er: YScO3 Laser Ceramic
abstract: The spectroscopic characterization of compositionally disordered (Er<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.072</inf>SC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.445</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.483</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> transparent ceramic was carried out. The sample was obtained using vacuum sintering of nano-sized particles produced by the laser ablation method. Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ ions in this ceramic feature strong inhomogeneous spectral broadening and intense mid-infrared luminescence.

articleTitle: Terahertz generation from femtosecond plasma channels
abstract: We measured and simulated frequency-angular distribution of terahertz emission from the plasma channel of a single-color filament biased by electrostatic field. Pronounced on-axis maximum of terahertz emission was observed for the electric field above 3.2 kV/cm. Directional diagrams of frequencies <1 THz reveal a flat-top shape due to the constructive interference of terahertz waves emitted by dipole local sources.

articleTitle: Anisotropic relaxation in NADH excited state studied by polarized pump-probe spectroscopy in water-1,2-propandiol solutions
abstract: We studied fast energy transfer processes in NADH excited states in water-l,2-propandiol solutions using recently developed polarization-sensitive modulation pump-probe technique. Linear dichroism in NADH excited states in 0% and 40% 1,2-propandiol were studied with a temporal resolution of about 0.3 ps and extremely high sensitivity. Fast picosecond anisotropic relaxation in NADH was observed at the first time. The effect observed was shown to be due to the rotation of the molecular transition dipole moment in the course of fast rearrangement of NADH nuclear configuration.

articleTitle: Eye safe laser rangefinder for transport safety
abstract: We develop an ultracompact and lightweight eyesafe laser rangefinder for distances up to 10 km. It uses 1 mJ Yb:Er:glass diode pumped passively Q-switched laser and InGaAs avalanche photodiode with time dependent gain management. It gives 0,5 m RMS accuracy at distances up to 5 km and 1 m RMS accuracy up to 8 km. The design is robust and vehicle capable. The dimensions are 90x60x40 mm, weight is 200 g. Repetition rate is up to 5 Hz. The device gives pulsed laser rangefinder performance in half-palm dimensions and robust design.

articleTitle: The role of leaking modes on dynamic range of amplitude and phase electro-optic light modulators
abstract: This research discusses the leaking modes as an important optical noise factor, that limits dynamic range and contrast in the electro-optic modulators. The simulation demonstrates that the power of leaking modes at the output port of a common Mach-Zehnder modulator consists a 10-15% of the main waveguide mode even for the open state. When it is closed the leaking modes power increases due to the energy conservation law, so even after a Fresnel reflection from the modulator crystal's border the crosstalk can reach about 0,1-1% of the input power.

articleTitle: Calibration problem in laser ektacytometry of red blood cells
abstract: the problem of measuring red blood cell deformability by laser diffractometry in a shear flow (ektacytome-try) is considered. A calibration equation is obtained that connects the geometric parameters of the isointensity line of the diffraction pattern with the level of light intensity on this line. A simplified algorithm for measuring the spread of red blood cell in deformability is proposed, which is applicable to blood samples with a symmetric distribution function in deformability.

articleTitle: 3D scaffolds biodegradation in vivo tracking: current state and prospects
abstract: Determination of the in vivo biocompatibility of various potential biomaterials is an actual and important task in biomedicine. Although numerous evaluation techniques were developed, one of the most widely used methods for in vivo biocompatibility evaluation remains a histological analysis of adjacent tissues and cell responses to the implant. However, these techniques require sacrificing animals at each time period of the evaluation. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop strategies for real-time and non-invasively monitoring in vivo degradation. Fluorescence-related imaging, optical coherence tomography, computed tomography, and THz spectroscopy and imaging can be used to achieve this task. Here we will consider the most novel and our own works in the area of in vivo biodegradation and perspectives of the use of the mentioned techniques.

articleTitle: Spectral broadening compensation in 35 ps Nd:YAG regenerative amplifier
abstract: We report on a technique of spectral broadening compensation in 35 ps Nd:YAG regenerative amplifier based on the implementation of X-cut KTP Pockels cell. At <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 5\ \text{mJ}$</tex> output energy the spectrum width was 0.1 nm compared to 0.3 nm that was with X-cut RTP Pockels cell.

articleTitle: Dependence of the optically pumped Ne*-He lasing threshold on the position of the pump beam
abstract: The dependence of pumping thresholds of the optically pumped Ne*-He laser on the position of the pump beam between the electrodes was obtained for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{s}_{5}\rightarrow \mathrm{p}_{9}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{s}_{5}\rightarrow$</tex> p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> pumping transitions. It was found that pumping thresholds strongly depended on the position of the pumping beam, and the minimum is reached near the center between the electrodes. The ratio of p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>/p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> thresholds at their minima is 13.

articleTitle: 40-meter postfilament evolution in air
abstract: We performed full characterization of postfilament formed by the radiation of the Ti: Sa laser system on an extended atmospheric path. Single-shot angle-wavelength spectra, beam diameter and self-correlation function measurements have been employed for this purpose. Using angle-wavelength spectra, the evolution of on-axis red-shifted humps has been traced, showing that their divergence does not exceed 0.5 mrad. Two zones in the postfilamentation process have been revealed: the Stockes zone with soliton-like propagation, where the number of the Stockes humps and their shift increases while the pulse duration remains almost constant, and the zone where the temporal and spectral postfilament characteristics changes like in linear propagation mode, while the beam divergence is negligible due to the Kerr nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Exotic Nonlinear Effects in Multimode Fibers
abstract: We experimentally and theoretically studied femtosecond laser pulse propagation with powers slightly below the breakdown threshold. In this regime, nonlinear absorption strongly affects spatio-temporal beam dynamics, and several exotic nonlinear optical effects are observed.

articleTitle: Optimal parameters for generation of extreme magnetic fields by relativistic intense circularly polarized laser pulse interacting with nanoclusters
abstract: Optimal parameters (density, radius) of a cluster target and laser pulse (intensity, duration) were found using analytical modelling and 3D PIC simulations, which make it possible to obtain a quasi-stationary magnetic field with an amplitude of several GGs. It is shown that a field of such strength slows down the thermal expansion of the cluster in the direction transverse to the laser beam axis

articleTitle: Nanostructured and molecular ROS generators for Photo- and Sonodynamic therapy
abstract: Sonodynamic therapy can dramatically enhance the efficiency of non-invasive tumor treatment due to multiple mechanisms initiating cell apoptosis or necrosis under ultrasound action combined with molecular and nanostructured sonosensitizers. Recently, we have demonstrated for the first time the sonodynamic effect of low-intensity 20 kHz ultrasound combined with chlorin e6 on melanoma cells.

articleTitle: Optical percutaneous needle biopsy to differentiate liver cancer from normal parenchyma
abstract: This work presents results of optical percutaneous needle biopsy to differentiate liver cancer from normal parenchyma in vivo and in situ measurements by two developed optical biopsy systems. The accuracy characteristics of optical systems are shown, technology development prospects are described.

articleTitle: Low-order harmonics generation driven by femtosecond mid-IR Fe: ZnSe laser system
abstract: The generation of low-order harmonics in the gas medium by femtosecond laser radiation of unique mid-IR Fe: ZnSe laser system operating at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.5\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> wavelength is investigated. The dependence of the harmonics generation efficiency on the experimental parameters is studied, that allows optimization of the harmonics yield. The present work is a new step towards high-order harmonics generation driven by low-frequency laser fields.

articleTitle: MBE growth and optical properties of InAs quantum dots in Si
abstract: Fabrication of nanocomposite materials consisting of III-V quantum dots (QDs) embedded in silicon (Si) sustained special attention over years. In this work, we present the formation of InAs QD in Si matrix by molecular beam epitaxy and the study of optical properties.

articleTitle: Influence of spatial characteristics of high-power quantum-cascade laser beams on the fiber-coupling efficiency
abstract: We study the influence of spatial characteristics of radiation of high-power mid-infrared quantum-cascade lasers on the efficiency of coupling to the optical fiber.

articleTitle: Synthesis and properties of fluorescent folate modified polymer nanoparticles
abstract: In the last decade, great scientific interest has been focused on the development of folic acid (FA) modified nanomaterials, which is highly specific for interaction with folate cell receptors. The FA modification of existing nanoparticles is a complex multi-stage process requiring additional purification steps. Therefore, the most promising direction is to obtain the synthesis of fluorescence labels modified by FA in one stage, which can be carried out by the hydrothermal synthesis method.

articleTitle: Laser welding of borosilicate glass using by femtosecond fiber lasers
abstract: The work shows the principal possibility laser welding borosilicate glass using by IPG Photonics femtosecond fiber lasers. The main physical mechanisms of laser glass welding are considered. It is shown that laser welding of glass or transparent dielectrics is based on the mechanisms of nonlinear absorption high-intensity laser radiation. The main technological features of the process laser welding of borosilicate glass are demonstrated. Shear lap tests of the obtained welds were carried out, the load was over 100 MPas.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of quantum noise suppression of light in bismuth-modified tellurite fibers
abstract: Optical sources of squeezed quantum light are required for various ultraprecise measurements. For fiber-based Kerr squeezing technologies, silica fibers are widely used. Here an alternative fiber made of highly-nonlinear bismuth-modified tellurite glass is considered. We performed quantum dynamical simulations and analytical estimations and showed the possibility of attaining high quantum noise suppression up to -15 dB.

articleTitle: Anomalous changes in the band gap of ZnO during the oxidation of zinc nanoparticles
abstract: Granulated zinc metal films on fused quartz and sapphire supports were obtained via pulsed laser deposition and then oxidized in air. We found that the properties of the formed ZnO nanostructured film depend on the oxidation temperature and the nature of the film support in a complicated way. The reduced dimension of the zinc oxide nanoparticles manifests itself in the enhanced optical band gap.

articleTitle: Digital diaphanoscopy data processing for differentiation of maxillary sinus pathologies
abstract: The paper presents the results of the use of the digital diaphanoscopy method to detect the pathology of the maxillary sinuses with the participation of conditionally healthy volunteers and patients with various types of pathological changes, confirmed by CT results. The results sinuses state classifying based on a quantitative assessment of the registered scattering patterns of light are also presented.

articleTitle: Spectral properties of coupled silica microresonators
abstract: We theoretically studied mode hybridization of two coupled optical silica microresonators with whispering gallery modes (WGMs). Output spectra and supermode electric field distributions were calculated for various geometric parameters. For microresonators with slightly different diameters the coupling of the fundamental and non-fundamental WGMs was observed, leading to asymmetry in the spectra and the spatial field distributions of the supermodes.

articleTitle: Magneto-optical materials for Faraday isolators operating at the laser wavelength of ~2 µm
abstract: Faraday isolators are the essential components of complex laser systems. High-power laser radiation greatly affects the FI characteristics, thereby significantly narrowing the choice of magneto-optical materials. The report provides an overview of promising magneto-optical materials for the manufacture of magneto-optical elements of Faraday isolators operating at the laser radiation ~2µm, results of recent studies of their properties, and some results of the study of the realized Faraday isolators based on such materials.

articleTitle: Orbital part of the transverse component of the Poynting vector of fundamental mode and low loss regimes in solid core photonic crystal fibers
abstract: Loss dependence of the fundamental mode (FM) on wavelength for all solid band gap fibers (ASBGs) have a sharp decrease at certain set of ASBGF geometric parameters. At the same time, losses in holey fibers (HFs) change monotonically. This difference in behavior of leakage loss is determined by singularities arising in orbital part of the transverse Poynting vector in ASBGF.

articleTitle: Dispersion of Principal Refractive Indices of Monoclinic MgWO4 Laser Host Crystal
abstract: Magnesium tungstate, MgWO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, is a promising laser host crystal. MgWO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> is monoclinic and optically biaxial. We have studied the dispersion of its principal refractive indices, np < nm < n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>, in the spectral range of 0.53 – 1.06 µm. MgWO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> possesses high refractive index and a strong natural birefringence. np = 1.981, nm = 2.016 and ng = 2.167 at~ 1.06µm.

articleTitle: A Method For Forming A Tubular Beam Of Radially Polarized Laser Radiation
abstract: A method and a device for forming a tubular beam of radially polarized laser radiation with a limited or increased number of modes have been developed. The basis of an optical quantum generator consists of a hollow thin-walled active element with end faces in the form of Brewster cones at the large bases. The output mirror has an axicon surface with a Brewster angle at the base. A highly reflective mirror can be made either in the form of a sphere to generate a beam with a limited number of modes, or in the form of a truncated cone to form a beam with an increased number of modes.

articleTitle: Optoacoustic measurement of the mid-IR laser pulse properties
abstract: We present the single-shot optoacoustic method of the TEMoo mode laser pulse parameters retrieval (pulse duration and beam radius). The experimental proof of the concept is demonstrated with the use of Er:YAG mid-IR nanosecond laser radiation. The proposed method can be applied for any laser wavelength provided that the appropriate highly-absorptive medium was chosen. The presented method can be a subject of interest in the area of laser metrology and applications.

articleTitle: Influence of inelastic collisions on the efficiency of optical pumping of alkali atoms in a gas cell
abstract: We study the processes of optical pumping of alkali metal atoms in the gas cell with buffer gas for the quantum magnetometers. The value of pumped magnetic moment is strongly influenced by the collision effects. Collisions of alkali atoms with the buffer gas lead to partial destruction of the atomic quantum state. As a first approximation, we can assume that the state of electronic shell collapses, but the state of the nucleus is saved. This work is devoted to the description of this effect and its impact to the polarization of the magnetic moment.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic detection of pigments in tissues: correlation with tissue aging and cancer development
abstract: The direct calculation of the absorption coefficient spectra of various tissues from spectral measurements allowed to retrieve the contents of melanin and lipofuscin. In the rabbit brain cortex, 1.8 times higher melanin content is explained by the neuron degeneration process. Similar melanin and lipofuscin contents were found in the rabbit pancreas as a result of the tissue aging process. The conversion of 83 % of the melanin in the human normal kidney into lipofuscin in the cancer kidney indicates that lipofuscin can be considered a kidney cancer marker in humans.

articleTitle: Downhole Analyzer of Fluid
abstract: We introduce a downhole optical fluid analyzer for a fraction, component and phase composition of the formation fluids. Key features are extreme downhole operation conditions at + 150C and 100 MPa. The solutions for several complicated optoelectronic cases are discussed below.

articleTitle: Single- and Multi-soliton generation in ANDi-laser with tunable spectral filtration
abstract: We investigated the influence of spectral filtration inside all-normal dispersion (ANDi) fiber mode-locked laser on dissipative soliton formation. The circular fiber cavity with semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) and tunable spectral filter was chosen as experimental platform. It was found that central wavelength of the spectral filter significantly influences on whether single or multi-soliton regime would be generated. Depending on matching between net spectral losses of the laser cavity and filter spectral profile it is possible to generate from 1 to 3 solitons inside optical bunch.

articleTitle: Targeted silver nanoparticles for cancer phototherapy and diagnostics
abstract: To obtain targeted nanoagents for phototherapy, we have synthesized silver nanoparticles of various shapes, including spheres, nanorods, nanoprisms, and nanowires. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, optical spectroscopy, and dynamic light scattering. We have developed a number of methods for modifying and stabilizing nanoparticles with recombinant proteins and polymers. We have obtained targeted nanoagents based on silver particles and proteins (antibodies or scaffold proteins) that can selectively bind cancer cells. We have demonstrated the possibility of silver nanoparticle application as photosensitizers using various light sources.

articleTitle: Investigation of Amplified Spontaneous Emission Broadband Sources Based on C and L-band Er-doped Fibers
abstract: In this article, we compare various schemes for constructing a broadband source with amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), for subsequent use as a master source for a distributed temperature monitoring system on Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: Plasma prepared nanostructured complex oxide materials for advanced UV-visible detectors
abstract: Oxide semiconductors for ultraviolet (UV) - visible detection have attracted attention in recent years. The extreme sensitivity and resolution of these materials, as well as their radiation resistance, are grounds for their potential widespread use in various applications.

articleTitle: Cumulative Terahertz Emission from a Magnetized Cherenkov Wake
abstract: We propose a scheme for cumulative ejection of narrowband terahertz radiation generated by a powerful laser driver in a magnetized plasma column. The radiation propagating in the plasma at different angles to the laser path is cumulated by a pair of dielectric prisms of total internal reflection and ejected from the prisms collinearly to the laser beam with high efficiency.

articleTitle: Photodynamic therapy with 5-ALA induced PpIX effect on macrophages polarization
abstract: In this work, we have carried out the assessment of changes in the polarization of macrophages in response to photodynamic treatment according to the changes in the fluorescence lifetime of respiratory chain enzymes. The analysis of the time-resolved fluorescence of metabolic signatures and PpIX makes it possible to determine the cell metabolism types.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics in twisted multicore fibers with PT-symmetry
abstract: Linear and nonlinear modes of PT-symmetric multicore fibers twisted around the central axis are studied. We determine the spectral properties of such systems and show that the presence of a central core and twist can significantly change the mode structure, as well as the PT-symmetry breaking threshold. We also construct stationary nonlinear modes and investigate their stability.

articleTitle: Optical characterization of CdTe/CdMgTe quantum well structure containing ultrathin manganese layers at interfaces
abstract: The aim of this work was to grow and study the optical properties of heterostructures with ultrathin inclusions at interfaces, which improve the quality of interfaces.

articleTitle: Morphological changes of red blood cell trapped in laser tweezers
abstract: The main goal of this work was to investigate the impact of a laser trap produced by a strongly focused laser beam of laser tweezers on a red blood cell (RBC). The RBC shape changes during trapping were found for numerous powers in the beam waist. The obtained results can be useful in the enlightenment of problems of interaction of laser beams with RBC.

articleTitle: Internal reference method for the study of upconversion luminescence of nanoparticle suspensions
abstract: This paper presents a new internal reference method for studying the upconversion luminescence of nanoparticle suspensions. The method provides correct analysis and comparison of luminescent signals obtained under different conditions. For excitation of the signal it is proposed to use the radiation of optical parametric oscillator at two wavelengths in order to simultaneously excite the upconversion luminescence of nanoparticles and the Raman signal of the medium in the Stokes region. Raman signal plays role of internal reference which allows to eliminate the influence of the instability of excitation intensity, inaccuracy of experimental setup adjustment etc. on the result of measurements.

articleTitle: RBC interaction with endothelial cells: study using laser tweezers technique
abstract: This work aimed to measure the interaction force between single red blood cells and endothelial cells using laser tweezers and a microfluidic channel. We found that the cells interaction forces depend on the concentration of fibrinogen and other factors activating the interaction in the environmental medium. This finding is important for understanding the basic mechanisms of red blood cells interaction with vascular endothelium.

articleTitle: The use of THz metamaterials for studying the adsorption of the SARS-CoV-2 virus spike protein by vibrational spectroscopy
abstract: Adhesion of the SARS-CoV-2 virus spike protein was studied by vibrational spectroscopy using terahertz metamaterials. Specific features of metastructure absorption by histidine, albumin, and receptor-binding domain of spike protein films were investigated. An original method for quantitative estimation of the efficiency of virus adhesion on the surface of metamaterials has been proposed and experimentally tested.

articleTitle: Energy and momentum of electromagnetic field in media with nonlocality of nonlinear optical response
abstract: We discuss the analytical expressions for energy density, Poynting vector, momentum density and momentum flux density of electromagnetic field in media with spatial dispersion of nonlinear optical response in first approximation to spatial dispersion parameter. These quantities are obtained in slowly varying envelope approximation.

articleTitle: Measuring the “backflash” probability of a single-photon detector with a time correlator
abstract: We present an experimental setup for the research of photon re-emission (“backflash”) of a single-photon detector depending on the time parameters. The uniqueness of this experimental setup with a time correlator lies in the very low amount of dark and parasitic noise, as well as in the negligibly small contribution of reflected photons in the histograms obtained. Thus, the signal-to-noise ratio increases by at least two orders of magnitude compared to the “classical” optical reflectometry scheme. Histograms of the distribution of “backflash” counts were obtained with a resolution of 100 ps per bin.

articleTitle: Evaluation of vascularization parameters of experimental tumors of different morphogenesis
abstract: Using OA and DOS the comparison of vascular structure and oxygenation of renal (SN-12C) and colon (Colo320, HCT116) cancer models was carried out. High vascularity was found for Colo320 and SN-12C as compared to HCT116. For Colo320 the presence of extended hemoglobin-containing structures was revealed, as well as a significantly decreased level of oxygenation.

articleTitle: 220 nm Wideband, 1.45 µm Band Wavelength-Swept Laser with Two Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers
abstract: We report 1.45 µm band wavelength-swept laser using two semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) and a polygonal mirror scanning wavelength filter. We have achieved 220 nm scanning bandwidth from 1348 nm to 1568 nm.

articleTitle: Thermodynamic Analysis of Borate Formation in the Synthesis of Glass-Ceramics Based on BaO – B2O3 – Bi2O3 and Er:YAG
abstract: The temperature conditions for the formation of aluminum, yttrium, erbium, barium, and bismuth borates from the glass-ceramic phase were determined by the Gibbs energy minimization method. The use of thermodynamic information in the interpretation of the results of thermal, XRD, and SEM analyzes of glass-ceramic samples contributed to the optimization of the modes of their sol-gel synthesis.

articleTitle: Palm-size dual-microcomb source
abstract: For the first time we demonstrate dual-comb source based on electrically driven broadband (till 300nm) Kerr-microcombs generated using high-Q SiN microresonators and self-injection locked semiconductor laser diodes emitting at the C-band telecom range. Prospect include chip-scale devices for broadband absorption spectroscopy, ranging application and multiplex data acquisition with many comb lines. Introduced palm-size device provides microcombs of ∼mWs power level and comprising commercially available photonic chips and laser diodes that can be used for out-of-the lab and industrial dual-comb applications.
