abstract: In the current study are investigated pigmented skin neoplasia - benign, dysplastic and malignant ones using Near- Infrared fluorescence technique and diffuse - reflectance spectroscopy in order to make them easier to distinguish.

articleTitle: Features of transmission of terahertz radiation by a nonlinear Fabry-Perot interferometer
abstract: Transmission of the Fabry-Perot interferometer with nonlinear media can be bistable. In this work the numerical results show that bistable transmission of nonlinear Fabry-Perot interferometer in terahertz spectral range is achievable already when thickness of the nonlinear media is comparable to radiation wavelength.

articleTitle: Synthesis and spectroscopic studies of nanostructures based on upconversion nanoparticles coated with a photosensitizer for photodynamic therapy with infrared excitation
abstract: In this work, we studied the processes of energy transfer from upconversion nanoparticles to photosensitizer molecules. The possibility of photodynamic therapy with infrared excitation using synthesized nanostructures has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Free Carrier Absorption Measurement in Mid-Infrared Quantum Cascade Lasers
abstract: Free carrier absorption is one of the main parameters affecting the threshold current and optical power in quantum cascade lasers. We demonstrate the technique that allows to measure these optical losses in mid-infrared laser cavity.

articleTitle: As-Se: Yb thin films for active Mid-IR optical elements
abstract: The plasma deposition was utilized for creation of IR active As-Se layers doped with Yb in the range of 1–8 at.%. Dependence of the photoluminescence on the components' stoichiometry of the planar structures was also figured out.

articleTitle: Experimental and Simulative Analysis of Cladding-Pumped EYDFA Gain Evolution
abstract: Signal gain evolution of a cladding-pumped single-core erbium-ytterbium co-doped fiber amplifier (EYDFA) at different doped fiber lengths is analyzed. The research is performed both experimentally and using a simulation model based on the measured signal parameters and EYDF characteristics. The results are compared to estimate the possibility of using such simulations for gain characteristics prediction prior to EYDFA experimental implementation.

articleTitle: Dual-band two-photon excited photoluminescence from the doped $\text{Yb}^{3+}:\text{CsPbCl}_{\mathrm{x}}\text{Br}_{3-\mathrm{x}}$ perovskite nanocrystals
abstract: All-inorganic lead halide perovskite nanocrystals doped with ytterbium demonstrate dual-band emission with visible band tunable by halide ratio change. Both visible and near infrared emissions can be excited via two-photon absorption by the perovskite matrix. It should be noted that the energy transfer from the perovskite matrix to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Yb}^{3+}$</tex> center is nonlinear and depends on temperature and excitation power.

articleTitle: Transverse magnetophotonic intensity effect in plasmonic nanostructures with broken spatial symmetry
abstract: The transmittance of any nanostructure can be controlled by proper engineering of its dielectric and spatial properties. Applied magnetic field determines the dielectric properties of the ferrimagnetic nanostructures as well. We address the transverse magnetooptical intensity effect in two types of the nonsymmetric plasmonic nanostructures. It is shown that the effect depends on the asymmetry of the structure.

articleTitle: Optical properties of optically dense medium of alkali atoms having a nonzero temperature under conditions of coherent population trapping resonance detected by the Ramsey method
abstract: A mathematical model of the interaction of bichromatic pulsed laser radiation with an optically dense medium of alkali atoms at a nonzero temperature is constructed. A numerical scheme for solving the obtained integro-differential equations is proposed. The results of the solution are analyzed for the dependence of the shape and shifts of the obtained two-photon resonances on temperature.

articleTitle: Squeezed light generation via frequency degenerate parametric down-conversion with cascaded up-conversion
abstract: We present the results of the analytical and numerical analysis of the generation of squeezed states via frequency-degenerate PDC with CUpC. We demonstrate the dynamics of the quadrature squeezing of the PDC and CUpC modes inside the nonlinear crystal. With the use of Reid criterion we show the conditions, when PDC and CUpC modes are entangled or separable.

articleTitle: Optical Label-Free Method for Characterization of Kinetics of Antibodies to SARS-CoV-2
abstract: To date, a dangerous infectious disease of COVID-19 caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-Co V -2) has been a significant source of morbidity and high mortality worldwide. In this work, an optical label-free method is developed for measurements and characterization of kinetics of antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 in real time. A biomarker of COVID-19, namely, spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 antigen was used as a model antigen. The proposed method employs inexpensive and widely available consumables compatible with various chemical interfaces. It is promising for assessment the kinetics of humoral response to SARS-CoV-2 infection or postvaccination.

articleTitle: 1-kHz nanosecond DPSS conductive cooling Nd:YAG laser for femtosecond pulses amplification
abstract: A nanosecond diode-pumped Nd:YAG laser with pulse repetition rate up to 1 kHz without liquid cooling of the of the active media has been demonstrated. The laser provided the following parameters: pulse width 8 ns (FWHM), pulse energy 10 mJ at 1064 nm and up to 4 mJ at 532 nm.

articleTitle: Investigation of bend loss in multimode core-shell silver halide MIR fibres
abstract: In this paper, we describe the experimental study of bend losses in single-layer multimode silver halide polycrystalline fibres in a PEEK shell bent into a circle. The experiment was conducted for Ø 525-µm AgBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf> fibre over the bend radius range of 1.5-52.5 mm for the wavelength sweep of 4–25 µm, The revealed dependencies can be very useful for designing fibre-optic systems intended for measurements in restricted spaces.

articleTitle: Physical aspects and possibilities of laser drug delivery
abstract: The features of active laser delivery of modern chlorin-containing photosensitizing drugs under the nail plate and skin are discussed. The delivery was carried out by simultaneous microperforation of the nail plate and stimulation of laser-induced hydrodynamic processes in the drug applied to the nail surface. The optimal parameters for microporation and active laser delivery of drugs were determined. The results of studying the absorption spectra of modern chlorin-containing photosensitizing drug “Chloderm” in the range of 400÷900 nm before and after exposure to radiation with a wavelength of 450 nm, 654 ± 10 nm and 2810 nm are presented.

articleTitle: Laser beam quality M2factor measurement: transport-of-intensity approach potential
abstract: A straightforward method based on a solution of the transport-of-intensity equation for laser beam quality M2 factor measurement is presented. Demonstrated experimental results prove that the approach is valid. Reconstruction of the other laser beam spatial parameters is presented, namely: radius, waist position, angular divergence, Rayleigh length and quality parameter.

articleTitle: Effective Fluorescence Control for TUR of the Bladder
abstract: We present here the effective video-fluorescence diagnosis with laser excitation at 635 nm with subsequent TUR of the bladder. After the diagnosis, the main tumor foci were resected first, and then a fluorescence analysis of the tumor borders was performed. Small fluorescing tumor tissues, not seen by cystoscopy in white light, were detected and the diagnostic fluorescence contrast was measured to quantify 5-ALA in tissues. The endoscopic images, registering the tumors, are very important in the development of signal processing techniques in augmented reality mode or mosaic mapping of the obtained series of images.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of a unitary transformation of an integrated interferometer using coherent light
abstract: Integrated optics fastens its place in taken important part of most promising fields of technology including communication and optical modulators, optical neural networks and quantum computing. Once optical integrated chip is fabricated it is essential to characterize its unitary transformation. The unitary provides a complete knowledge about chip operation. Therefore, trustful methods of chip transformation reconstruction are of interest. Here we have performed unitary transformation reconstruction of the femtosecond laser written optical chip with coherent light.

articleTitle: Self-sweeping Er-doped ring fiber laser with sweeping direction control
abstract: We present here a self-sweeping Er-doped ring fiber laser generating near 1606 nm with possibility of sweeping rate and direction control by pump power variation. Reverse and normal self-sweeping operations with sweeping rates of -1 and 0.5 pm/s are observed at low and high pump powers respectively. The developed laser source can be in demand for sensor applications.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of collinear and noncollinear schemes for coherent combining of high-power few-cycle femtosecond pulses
abstract: We present the results of studies on the optimization of coherent combining schemes for high-power pulses in collinear and noncollinear geometries, a comparative analysis of the requirements on the parameters of the combined pulses to achieve high efficiency of coherent combining.

articleTitle: Time-lapse microscopy of polyamine-immobilized diatoms: towards novel biosensors
abstract: We present a low-cost biomonitoring system based on the movement of diatom organelles and diatom replication. Monitoring of organelle motion in the immobilized mother cell, unbound thecae structure and offspring cells provide multi-factor insight to environment composition. The monitoring, data analysis and data transfer require only a smartphone, a lens-clip and a replaceable “cartridge” with a microfluidic circuit and immobilized cells.

articleTitle: Improving the efficiency of terahertz antennas on topological insulators
abstract: We study photoconductive antennas based on thin film of topological insulator and semiconductor heterostructure. A shift of the spectrum of a dipole antenna on a topological insulator to the long-wavelength region was found in comparison with a similar semiconductor antenna. Ways to increase the efficiency due to the deposition of plasmon gratings, as well as controlling the frequency response by changing the antenna impedance will be discussed.

articleTitle: InGaAs/InGaAsP/InP heterostructures for high-power photodetectors
abstract: A UTC photodetector based on InGaAs/InGaAsP/InP heterostructures grown by MOCVD is demonstrated. A model of the band diagram of the photodetector is proposed. Energy barriers that reduce the rate of hole removal from the absorbing layer are shown. A solution to reduce these barriers and increase the holes velocity is proposed.

articleTitle: Multicomponent chalcogenide Pb-based thin films for Mid-IR photodetectors
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PbS}_{1-\mathrm{x}}\text{Se}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> films of different macro-content and phase morphology were prepared by Plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition. The selenium content has a considerable influence on resistivity, carrier concentration, and carrier mobility in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PbS}_{1-\mathrm{x}}\text{Se}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> films.

articleTitle: Determination of biotissue photodegradation kinetic parameters based on electrical impedance
abstract: A method for determination of degradation kinetic parameters in laser damage process of biological tissues is proposed. By scattering of laser radiation, homogeneous heating of the sample was created. In this process the temperature dependence of its low-frequency electrical impedance (~ 1 kHz) was measuring. By processing these kinetics with Arrhenius formulations such important parameters of the heating kinetics as critical temperatures and activation energies were obtained.

articleTitle: Comparative study of the endovenous laser coagulation with 1.47 and 1.94 μm clinical effiscacy
abstract: There are presented results of clinical effectiveness comparative study of use endovenous laser coagulation with wavelengths of laser light λ=1.47 and 1.94 μm for treatment of varicose veins. Studies have shown that EVLT with a wavelength of λ= 1.94 μm is accompanied by significantly less intraoperative pain syndrome and the risk of skin hyperpigmentation in the target vein projection. A lower penetration depth at wavelength λ= 1.94 μm reduces the risk of thermal damage to the nerve trunks near the target vein.

articleTitle: Dependence of Radachlorin fluorescence lifetime on solution pH and localization in Hela cells
abstract: Variations of Radachlorin fluorescence lifetime with pH in PBS solutions have been studied. As shown, an increase in pH resulted in the fluorescence lifetime rise. FLIM-assisted experiments on Radachlorin fluorescence lifetimes in living HeLa cells demonstrated dependence of the lifetime on intracellular localization of Radachlorin molecules. Recorded variations of Radachlorin fluorescence lifetime within intracellular area were about 15-20%.

articleTitle: Ultra-wide spectral range X-ray diagnostics of relativistic femtosecond laser plasma
abstract: The X-ray emission of relativistic laser plasma was investigated in the spectral range from XUV to gammas by a set of detectors and techniques. Thermal and hot electron components generation was studied in dependence of the peak laser intensity and contrast of the laser pulse.

articleTitle: Efficient Cherenkov-Type Optical-to-Terahertz Conversion of nJ-Energy Femtosecond Laser Pulses
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally that a sandwich-like structure comprising a thin layer of lithium niobate clamped between two Si prisms of total internal reflection can serve as an efficient converter of nJ-energy level laser pulses from a femtosecond optical oscillator to a high-quality beam of broadband terahertz radiation. The converter has an additional advantage of workability at different laser wavelengths.

articleTitle: Mid-IR Spectroscopic Sensing Based on Mulitmode Chalcogenide Fibers
abstract: Theoretical and technological peculiarities of creating a multimode chalcogenide fiber based platform for the remote real time mid-IR spectroscopy of liquids are discussed.

articleTitle: Module-designed picosecond Nd:YAG laser for high-precision satellite laser ranging
abstract: We report on the development of picosecond Nd:YAG laser applied for high precision satellite laser ranging. Laser generates 35 ps pulses at 532 nm wavelength with 2.5 mJ pulse energy and 500 Hz pulse repetition rate. The main feature of the developed system is modular design.

articleTitle: Differential laser atmospheric remote sensing system for environmental monitoring
abstract: The relevance of the study is due to the need for remote monitoring of the atmosphere for the presence of suspended substances. The use of this method for geological exploration will allow identifying areas with a high content of suspended substances in the atmosphere, which will allow registering local natural gas outputs, as well as observing the spatial dynamics of surface leaks in real time, carrying out topographic mapping of promising deposits, etc. In addition, the detection of leaks and increased concentrations of methane will allow for the early implementation of a set of measures aimed at preventing environmental disasters.

articleTitle: Imaging Flow Cytometry for Investigation of Extracellular Vesicles-Magnetic Nanoparticles Interactions for Liquid Biopsy
abstract: A novel approach was developed for investigation of interactions between extracellular vesicles (EVs) and magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs). It combines high-resolution imaging flow cytometry (IFC) with fluorescently labeled MNP conjugates. The IFC data verified the optimality of parameters including the amount of MNP conjugates per test, duration of EV incubation with the conjugates for the efficient of magnetic immunochromatographic assay for liquid biopsy EV quantification.

articleTitle: Advanced microlasers and micro-optics enabled by femtosecond laser processing of halide perovskites
abstract: Chemically synthesized halide perovskites monocrystals hold promise for various advanced photonic and optoelectronic applications. However, their nanopatterning by standard lithography-based methods faces a number of problems related to impossibility of using liquid-phase pre- (post-) processing and worsening of their functional properties. In our work, we justified direct femtosecond-laser ablation of halide perovskite monocrystals as a highly efficient, flexible and non-destructive tool for their nanopatterning with a lateral resolution down to 150 nm. As a demonstration of the method applicability, we fabricated various reflection- and transmission-type micro-optics elements (Fresnel lenses, fork-shaped diffraction gratings and vortex beam generators) as well as holograms directly imprinted on the surface inorganic metal halide perovskite monocrystals. Also, we achieve directional lasing from a single perovskite nanowire by laser printing a nanograting on its top face that provided stimulated emission outcoupling to the vertical direction with a divergence angle around 2°.

articleTitle: Measurement of optical absorption coefficient of lithium triborate under the high-power CW laser radiation with Pierce oscillator circuit
abstract: We introduced a method for optical absorption of nonlinear optical crystals measurement based on a piezoelectric resonance laser calorimetry. Nonlinear crystal under examination is used as a frequency selective element in a feedback loop of RF oscillator circuit. Thus, resonance frequency is easily determined. Proposed method along with the conventional piezoelectric resonance laser calorimetry were used to measure optical absorption coefficient of litihium triborate crystal under high-power cw laser radiation.

articleTitle: Contribution of Collective Electron Dynamics to the Polarization Response of an Atom in Synchronized IR and XUV Pulses
abstract: We study the polarization response of different noble-gas atoms in an intense infrared (IR) laser field and a weak extreme ultraviolet (XUV) isolated attosecond pulse (IAP) based on the numerical solution of the time-dependent Kohn-Sham equations. Our numerical results show that collective multi-electron dynamics significantly enhance the polarizability of an atom, which makes possible the contribution of the elastic XUV re-emission channel to the atomic polarization response in combined IR and XUV fields. We show that the enhanced re-emission channel interferes with the IR-induced high harmonic generation channel and results in specific interference in the secondary radiation yield. Utilization of this interference for the phase retrieving of the generated harmonics in the IR field is discussed. The contribution of the third-order nonlinearity in XUV range to the total high-frequency response is shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Stimulated Absorption in Holmium Fibers in the Wavelength Range of $1.5-1.75\ \mu \mathrm{m}$
abstract: We study the excited-state absorption for holmium-doped optical fibers in the spectral range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.5-1.75\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The pump-induced absorption spectra and temporal transmission dynamics for fibers with different ion concentration and length are measured.

articleTitle: Simultaneous self-injection locking of two laser diodes to a single integrated microresonator
abstract: We both theoretically and experimentally investigate the dual-laser self-injection locking of two multifrequency laser diodes to different modes of an integrated Si3N4 microresonator. We observe simultaneous spectrum collapse of both lasers, as well as linewidth narrowing and high-frequency noise suppression, as well as strong nonlinear interaction of the two fields with each other. Simultaneous frequency and phase stabilization and coherent addition of output signal are observed for locking both lasers to the same mode.

articleTitle: Binary Two-Phase Gratings Formed on the Surface of Ge2Sb2Te5 Thin Film by Femtosecond Laser Pulses
abstract: The formation of binary amorphous-crystalline periodic structures on the surface of Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> thin film during a single pass of a femtosecond laser beam has been studied. We recorded biphase stripes up to several mm long consisted of 50 parallel amorphous/crystalline lines oriented perpendicular to the light polarization. These stripes had a period equal to the recording beam wavelength (1030 nm) and exhibited diffraction grating behavior due to the remarkable optical contrast. We performed diffraction simulations and obtained good agreement with the experimental results for a beam (532 nm) diffracted by the recorded grating.

articleTitle: Metrological studies of a digital autocollimator
abstract: The study of a digital autocollimator with two dimensional multi-element mark is considered in the report. 5 megapixel digital camera with a pixel size of 3.45 microns was used as a photoreceiver. The results showed that the error of the autocollimator is in the limit of 0.01 arc-sec.

articleTitle: Laser radiation at a wavelength of 525 nm used for controlled hemostasis
abstract: The results of exposure to laser radiation at a wavelength of 525 nm were studied and its parameters were determined for laser radiation to effectively stop bleeding.

articleTitle: Investigation of Volt-Ampere Characteristics of Crystalline Materials AgBr-AgI System
abstract: In this work, the dependence of the volt-ampere characteristics for optical infrared materials of the AgBr-AgI system solid solutions is studied depending on the composition of the material and temperature in the range of 298–423 K. It is established that an increase in the iodine content for crystalline materials of AgBr-AgI systems leads to a decrease in electrical conductivity.

articleTitle: Adaptive optics for aberration correction in PW lasers
abstract: The peculiar properties and principles of beam correction in pulsed lasers of PW power level are considered. Wide-aperture adaptive systems have been created to correct for aberrations and improve the focusing on the target. Bimorph deformable mirrors with free of “print-through” reflective surface and sizes of 320 and 400 mm have been developed, where the initial surface shapes after manual alignment were 1 and 1.5 µm (P- V), respectively. The use of an adaptive system with 320 mm deformable mirror in a 4.2 PW Ti: Sa laser provided a record intensity 1.lx1023 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> on the target when focusing by off-axis parabolic mirror f = 300 mm.

articleTitle: Powder and thin-film hybrid materials emitting in the IR-range, based on tris(8-hydroxyquinolate) Yb (III) in CaF2, PbF2 and PbO matrices
abstract: Organic-inorganic hybrid materials based on ytterbium (III) tris(8-hydroxyquinolate) were obtained in fluoride and oxide inorganic matrices by solid-phase synthesis. Thin films were prepared using the obtained powder hybrid materials by capillary deposition technique. The films demonstrated photoluminescence in the visible and infrared regions.

articleTitle: Gene and Small Molecule Delivery in vivo Using Novel Nanoparticle-based Systems
abstract: Combinatorial therapies based on co-delivery of drugs and nucleic acids have outstanding potential for improving therapy of socially significant diseases in comparison to standalone treatments. This encouraging approach gathers the activity of chemotherapeutics and nucleic acid capacity to repair deregulated signaling pathways, as a complex strategy to achieve a beneficial therapeutic effect. Nanoparticles are one of the most promising class of drug delivery vehicles due to their ability to simultaneously transport a great range and amount of payloads to achieve synergistic therapeutic effect. In this work, we demonstrate the possibility of adapting the properties of nanoparticles of various classes to deliver a wide range of therapeutic cargo for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: The Role of the Longitudinal Component of Electric Field for Evanescent Fiber-Optic Sensors
abstract: The role of the longitudinal electric field component in the evanescent fiber sensors is studied. Numerical methods are used to calculate the power transmission coefficient of two parallel optical fibers with taking into account the longitudinal component of the field. The dependence of the power transfer coefficient of two parallel optical fibers on the coupling length is obtained. It is demonstrated that the contribution of the longitudinal component of the field is significant for the calculation of evanescent sensors based on two optical fibers.

articleTitle: New Opportunities for Nanobiotechnology Based on Ultrasensitive Methods of Physical Measurements
abstract: Several ultrasensitive optical and magnetic methods have been developed for research in nanobiotechnology, for metrology of theranostic applications, medical diagnostic, food safety and environmental control, etc. Based on the developed hybrid magnetic nanoparticles and their quantification methods, the peculiarities of accumulation and biodegradation of various nanoparticles in animals in vivo have been revealed. New methods of significant enhancement (up to 50 times) of the nanoagent delivery to cancer tumors in animals have been proposed and experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Self-starting fiber mode-locked laser assisted with DDQN algorithm
abstract: Here, we investigate the performance of Double-Deep Q-learning (DDQL) algorithm for designing self-starting fiber laser. Fiber mode-locked laser based on nonlinear polarization effect was chosen as an experimental platform. We show that the proposed algorithm is capable to learn non-trivial hysteresis dynamics inside the laser in order to achieve stable soliton generation.

articleTitle: Pulse-periodical TEA-laser operating on a mixture of carbon dioxide and air
abstract: A variant of the TEA-CO2 laser with a closed cycle of transverse pumping of gas mixtures based on “CO2 - air”, operating at pulse repetition rates up to 1 kHz, has been implemented. With an active volume V <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$= 18\mathrm{x}0.8\mathrm{x}0.8\ \text{cm}^{3}$</tex>, the maximum average radiation power of 32 W at a pulse repetition rate of 600 Hz was achieved.

Author Keywords: laser radiation energy in a pulse

articleTitle: Double electron-electron resonance for investigation spin bath in diamond
abstract: NV-centers in diamonds are promising sensors of magnetic fields due to the possibility to control their state optically. The coherence of NV centers in diamond is limited by other paramagnetic impurities - C-centers. Unlike the NV- center, the C-center is a dark defect. This work demonstrates the detection, state control, and concentration determination of C-centers through their interaction with NV-centers.

articleTitle: Filtering Raman spectral features of glial tumor sites based on biochemical correlates
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is a sensitive and fast tool for analyzing the molecular composition of tissues, so we used it to differentiate glial tumor and normal tissues during surgery. The structure of Raman spectra motivated us to implement the feature selection technique, based on the filtering of those points of the spectrum for which statistically significant differences were found between the groups. Finally they were matched to the main biochemical components of the studied tissues, and new vectors of Raman features of a smaller dimension were formed.

articleTitle: Unipolar heterostructures with effective interband radiative recombination under current pumping
abstract: Design principles of isotype heterostructures for efficient interband recombination under electric current pumping are developed. Transport and radiative recombination features are studied for the InGaAs/AlGaAs/GaAs isotype heterostructure with the energy balance model. The radiative recombination current 43 A (with a pumping current 200 A) and the maximum internal quantum efficiency is 28% (at 55–65 A) were demonstrated in structures with 3 quantum wells. At currents above 15 A, the carrier density accumulated in the active region reaches a value of 3.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, which shows the possibility of unipolar laser diodes developing.

articleTitle: Mechanisms of Short Wavelength Light - Biological Tissue Interaction
abstract: The processes of formation and transfer of heat from exposure to short-wave infrared light - 1.5; 1.9 and (1.5 + 1.9) µm were studied in physiological solution, donor blood, and during interstitial thermotherapy of rabbit liver in vivo. Heat transfer corresponded to forced convection caused by boiling at the end of the fiber. The degree of damage to the intima of the liver vessels in the warming focus directly depended on their diameter.

articleTitle: Immunoglobulin-based hybrid targeted nanoagents for in vitro and in vivo multimodal imaging
abstract: Nanomedicine constantly broadens horizons of modern therapy and diagnostics. However, imaging nanoagents are of especial interest. Here, we report on novel, facile, and sustainable way to fabricate targeted multimodal imaging nanoparticles. Specifically, we synthesize nanoparticles using immunoglobulins and introduce nanoparticles of different nature into immunoglobulin-based matrix. We demonstrate applicability of the nanoparticles both in vitro and in vivo.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy properties of Dy3+ doped CaF2 single crystals and CaF2-SrF2 solid liquid
abstract: Samples of CaF2:D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>3+ crystals and CaF2-SrF2:D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>3+ solid solution were obtained by the Bridgman-Stockbarger method. The spectroscopic characteristics were calculated from the experimentally obtained optical spectra. Using the Judd-Ofelt analysis, intensity parameters 02,4,6 were obtained. On their basis, integral luminescence cross sections, radiative lifetimes, and luminescence branching coefficients in the IR region are calculated. Using the correspondence method, the luminescence spectra of the 6H13/2 -> 6H15/2 transition were obtained

articleTitle: Double wavelength laser source for a pulsed holography
abstract: The laser source with dual wavelengths, with tunable distance between them simultaneously generating is demonstrated. The possibility of using it for a two wavelength holography is shown. Dual wavelengths at 890.7 nm and 906.7 nm provides measured accuracy of 3d surface profile at 25 µm,

articleTitle: Femtosecond Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structuring of Metal and Semiconductor Nitrides
abstract: Highly regular thermochemical laser-induced periodic surface structures (TLIPSS) were produced on the surface of TiN, CrN and Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> glass-supported thin films using femtosecond IR- and visible-range laser pulses. Systematic studies of the TLIPSS morphology variation as a function of key laser processing parameters and ambient atmosphere revealed the processing regimes providing high-regular 2D and 3D morphologies promising for optical and optoelectronic applications.

articleTitle: Design of a space based telescope with variable beam direrction for a quantum communication link
abstract: The optical system of a satellite based telescope was designed. The resulting module has a variable output parallel beam angle and a near diffraction limited performance in the range of motion.

articleTitle: Thick-film SiN platform for hybrid integrated lasers
abstract: We report recent advances of the thick film SiN integrated photonics in general and particularly as a platform for hybrid lasers. Overview of the current technology state with relevant performance metrics is provided and the future outlook is discussed.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Texturing Amorphous Silicon Thin Films by Femtosecond Laser Irradiation
abstract: Femtosecond laser treatment allows to fabricate periodic structures at amorphous hydrogenated silicon surfaces on areas more than a square millimeter. The period of the structures is near the laser wavelength and determines by the nonequilibrium electrons concentration at high power laser excitation. The obtained structures possess a pronounced electrophysical anisotropy.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Structure and Impurity Composition of Synthetic HPHT Diamonds in the Process of Laser-Induced Surface Transformation
abstract: An analysis of the spectra of laser-induced plasma under multi-pulse exposure of a focused laser beam at each point under study on the surface of multi-sector diamond plates doped with nitrogen and boron was performed. A different degree of surface graphitization was found depending on the crystallographic orientation of the growth sectors, the type of doping element, and the degree of doping. The possibility of revealing the sectoral structure of samples and atomic structures, including impurity ones, with different strengths of interatomic chemical bonds is shown.

articleTitle: Microspherical lithography for selective epitaxy
abstract: The effect of focusing with microspheric lenses during the photolithography process is recently studied intensively due to the wide range of applications of this method. This paper presents the results of nanostructuring the silicon surface using photolithography on the hexagonal array of microspheric lenses and etching silicon in nanoholes. The possibility of epitaxial selective synthesis of semiconductor nanostructures A3B5 on silicon is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Phase-space topology of fiber four-wave mixing
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a new experimental testbed enabling the study and control of ideal four-wave mixing interactions in optics. Two approaches are used to reveal the phase-space topology of the underlying nonlinear processes. The first is based on iterated initial conditions in a short fiber segment. The second relies on an experimental dataset that is then processed and analyzed by a neural network.

articleTitle: Influence of waveguide composition on the efficiency of 940–980 nm InGaAs/AlGaAs/GaAs laser diodes
abstract: Approaches to improve the L- I characteristics of laser diodes emitting at 940–980 nm based on InGaAs/AlGaAs/GaAs separate confinement double heterostructures with an asymmetric broadened waveguide are studied. The influence of the waveguide composition on the lasers output characteristics is analyzed. It is shown that a decrease in the energy depth of the QW leads to a decrease in series and thermal resistances and cut-off voltage that allows to improve output characteristics.

articleTitle: Carrier-envelope phase of an elliptically polarized mid-IR light bullet
abstract: For the first time, the formation of a mid-IR single-cycle light bullet during propagation of a femtosecond laser pulse with an arbitrary initial polarization ellipticity of the light field has been experimentally and numerically investigated. It is established that the polarization ellipticity determines the effect of the carrier-envelope phase on the nonlinear-optical interaction of the light bullet with the medium.

articleTitle: High-power laser diodes with multiplied efficiency based on single transverse mode multi-junction heterostructures
abstract: A heterostructure design aimed at a multiple increase of the l060nm laser output efficiency is proposed. To multiply the internal and external quantum efficiency, tunnel p-n junctions (T J) were placed in the waveguide. Designed and MOCVD-grown heterostructures including two TJs demonstrate. Fabricated laser diodes demonstrate a stable second-order mode operation and a slope efficiency of 2.4W / A.

articleTitle: Decay of Induced Absorption in La0.05Gd0.95VO4 Crystal in Visible Spectral Region
abstract: Induced absorption in La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf>Gd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.95</inf>Vo4crystal under two-photon interband excitation by picosecond laser radiation at 523.5 nm was investigated. Temporal behavior of absorption revealed short and long decay stages and their dependence on initial value.

articleTitle: Coherent conversion between one and two photons in waveguides with engineered dispersion
abstract: High-efficiency photon-pair production is a long-sought-after goal for many optical quantum technologies, and coherent photon conversion processes are promising candidates for achieving this. We show theoretically how to control coherent conversion between a narrow-band pump photon and broadband photon pairs in nonlinear optical waveguides by tailoring frequency dispersion for broadband quantum frequency mixing.

articleTitle: Model of a Photosensitizer for Photodynamic Therapy Based on Upconversion Nanoparticles
abstract: Stable surface coating of the upconversion nanoparticles with human serum albumin (HSA) was carried out to cross-link the photodynamic dye with the particles.

articleTitle: Diffraction and selective properties of one-dimensional and two-dimensional periodic structures in a wide range of angles of incidence
abstract: The diffraction and selective properties of various types of periodic nanostructures in promising photopolymer materials at radiation incidence in a wide range of angles are presented for the creation on their basis of effective deflectors and laser beam splitters, as well as diffractive elements for solar energy.

articleTitle: Gain switching sub-ns pulse laser diode optimization for time-of-flight laser rangefinding
abstract: The problem of designing laser heterostructures for generating sub-ns laser pulses of a given duration with a maximum peak power in the gain-switching mode is considered. An algorithm for numerical multiparameter optimization based on lumped rate equations is proposed.

articleTitle: Optical properties of ceramics made of silver halide solid solutions doped with rare-earth elements
abstract: In this study, we investigated optical characteristics of transparent ceramics based on silver halide solid solutions doped with rare-earth elements such as neodymium and ytterbium. The results showed that such materials can be used for creating the sources of coherent radiation in the IR region.

articleTitle: Laser pulse shaping at third harmonic generation process
abstract: A new approach to generating triangular and cone-shaped laser pulses in UV region is proposed. It is based on third harmonic generation process at collinear interaction of 3D ellipsoidal and cylindrical chirped laser pulses in a nonlinear crystal.

articleTitle: Narrow linewidth lasing in Nd:YVO4 disk laser with two-mirror cavity with M-type degenerate configuration
abstract: Single-frequency lasing was realized in the continuous-wave TEMoo Nd:YVO4 disk laser with the two-mirror plane-spherical resonator. The laser cavity had degenerate M-type configuration without any intracavity wavelength selectors. Spectral, energy, and spatial characteristics of the laser output were studied. Also, the reasons of single-frequency lasing existence were proposed.

articleTitle: Growth of III-V nanowires by molecular beam epitaxy: the role of material exchange with the substrate
abstract: Growth theory of III-V nanowires fabricated by molecular beam epitaxy is developed to reveal the role of the substrate which can be either unpatterned or masked with an inert SiOx, layer. Axial and radial growths of nanowires are described in both cases, converging to the asymptotic stage which is independent of the substrate due to the shadowing effect. The nanowire lengths and radii are calculated as functions of time and the growth parameters. Good fits are obtained with the data on the growth kinetics of GaAs, GaP, InAs and InP nanowires.

articleTitle: Measurement of the absorption cross section of transitions in cesium and rubidium atoms using nonharmonic pumping
abstract: We consider and implement a method for measuring the absorption cross section <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> of alkali metal atoms pumped by radiation with a finite spectrum width. We demonstrate a comparison of the calculated and experimentally measured values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5S_{1/2}\rightarrow 6P_{3/2}$</tex> transition in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Rb$</tex> atoms that are in a good agreement taking into account the nonmonochromaticity of the pumping.

articleTitle: Fluorescence evaluation of tissue samples from skin collagen-related diseases
abstract: We have implemented excitation-emission matrices for fluorescence assessment of tissue samples from degenerative skin diseases. Those measurements are part of a proof of concept study for the development of a new technique for noninvasive optical diagnostic of degenerative skin diseases.

articleTitle: Effect of Polarisation on Optical Gain of InGaN/GaN Quantum Wells
abstract: III-nitride semiconductors are crucial for solid-state lighting applications, especially in the blue and ultraviolet regions. They have polarisation fields and charges inside them which modify their optoelectronic properties. In this article, we study the effect of the polarisation fields on the band structure and optical gain of an InGaN/GaN quantum well.

articleTitle: Shock-Ignition Inertial Fusion Energy Beam Profiling and Self-Focusing Mitigation at High-Power GARPUN KrF Laser
abstract: We propose to combine KrF laser pulse form for a shock-ignition Inertial Fusion Energy application by simultaneous amplification of short & long pulses, discuss an impact of self-focusing and filamentation in atmospheric air for laser beam phase randomization and spectra broadening, as well as mitigation of filamentation with a Xe cell.

Author Keywords: temporal pulse profiling for Shock Ignition Inertial Fusion Energy

articleTitle: Boosting MIR to THz conversion with tight focusing
abstract: 3D + time numerical simulations of terahertz (THz) generation in two-color femtosecond filament with the optimal phase between the optical harmonics reveal the non-monotonic dependence of the THz energy on the central wavelength of fundamental harmonic pulse. Tight focusing boosts up the conversion efficiency for the MIR pump thus making the THz energy increase monotonically with the wavelength.

articleTitle: Investigation of the characteristics of a microresonator with carbon nanotubes deposited on its surface
abstract: Nonlinearity of carbon nanotubes significantly exceeds nonlinearity of the materials of crystal. Deposition of carbon nanotubes to the surface of the microresonator may enhance its nonlinearity. In this paper, the characteristics of high-quality factor microresonators with whispering gallery modes with single walled carbon nanotubes deposited on the surface are experimentally investigated.

articleTitle: Performance of InGaAs/GaAs Microdisk Lasers with Improved Thermal Resistance
abstract: We discuss the static characteristics and high-frequency performance of microdisk lasers with an active region based on dense array of InGaAs/GaAs quantum well-dots having the improved thermal resistance. The decrease in thermal resistance of the microlasers is achieved by epi-side down bonding on a heat-conducting Si substrate. Compared to the characteristics of initial microlasers, the bonding results in a in thermal resistance decreasing by a factor of 2.3 (1.8) in microdisks with a diameter of 19 (31)µm, Further improvement of heat removal is achieved by a thinner epitaxial structure between the active region and the heatsink, realized by concept of two coupled resonant planar waveguides. Using this method, we managed to place the active region at a distance of only 870 nm from the surface of the heterostructure and achieve the record low thermal resistance of 0.17 K/mW in bonded lasers.

articleTitle: $\delta^{13}\mathrm{C}$ measurements in a human exhalation
abstract: The ratio of stable 13C/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>C carbon isotopes in the exhaled human breath was measured and compared to a standard value of reference material. Extended uncertainty of measurements was calculated. The factors influencing the measurement's uncertainty in the Raman spectroscopy analysis of the gas mixture's quantitative composition were determined.

articleTitle: Novel Approaches in 3D Live Cell Microscopy
abstract: Novel approaches and devices for 3D live cell imaging are reported. They include 3D printed devices for localization of samples in a microscope as well as axial tomography for obtaining a high isotropic resolution.

articleTitle: Six European XFEL scientific instruments
abstract: The European X-Ray Free-Electron Laser (European XFEL) is a research facility that opens the way to unprecedented time (up to 15 fs) and spatial resolution. This review contains a short description of the 6 European XFEL instruments and studies implemented on them.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Photoplethysmographic Waveform by Monte Carlo Simulation of Light Transport
abstract: The photoplethysmographic waveform was modeled for different source-detector distances using the Monte Carlo technique. For this, a three-layer optical model of the skin for reflection was developed. It was found that the pulse wave is most pronounced for the distance of 6 mm.

articleTitle: Ultrashort Pulse Raman Conversion 1.03→3.9 µm in a gas-filled Revolver Hollow-Core Silica Fiber
abstract: Efficient generation at 3.9 micron is demonstrated via Raman conversion of 1.03-micron ultrashort laser pulses in a gas-filled hollow-core silica fiber.

articleTitle: X-ray diagnostics of laser-induced plasma embedded in strong magnetic field with a varied orientation
abstract: The present work is aimed at the experimental study of the dynamics of laser-induced plasma immersed in a strong poloidal magnetic field with a variable orientation (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}-90^{\circ}$</tex> depending on the plasma expansion) and amplitude (up to 30 T). The significance of such studies is especially important for the tasks of laboratory astrophysics and inertial confinement fusion. Electron density and temperature profiles are measured, effects related with plasma collimation, accumulation, as well as separation, generation of instabilities and shocks by the magnetic field are discussed.

articleTitle: DIY plasma system for PDMS labs-on-a-chip
abstract: We present a low-cost DIY plasma activation system suitable for irreversible bonding PDMS to PDMS or glass substrates and changing the surface properties of materials.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum Generation In Fiber Amplifiers And Its Partial Amplification
abstract: The supercontinuum generation in the wavelength range 1000–2400 nm in silica-based fibers with output power 340 mW is presented. Spectral and temporal irradiation conversions in three different fiber amplifiers (erbium-doped, thulium-doped and holmium-doped fiber amplifier) have been investigated.

articleTitle: Modeling of laser vibrometer-rangefinder based on self-sweeping Yb-doped fiber laser
abstract: We present a scheme for the simultaneous measurement of the absolute distance to the target and its vibrations. The vibration effects modeling is carried out and the influence of tuning laser stability is discussed.

articleTitle: Multiterawatt laser pulse conversion into THz range: nonlinear crystals vs gas plasma
abstract: 2-10 TW laser pulses are converted into THz range with relatively high efficiency in two schemes: large aperture thin nonlinear crystals (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and GaSe) and low pressure, two-color gas discharge. 2–10 uJ energy pulse in THz range is obtained with tunable bandwidth up to 6 THz. Advantages of phase matched and non-matched THz generation near the breakdown threshold of thin crystals are discussed.

articleTitle: Manganese concentration effect on spectral properties of lithium-zinc-germanate glass-ceramics
abstract: The spectral properties of lithium-zinc-germanate glass-ceramics doped with different manganese content are investigated. Luminescence spectra contain two bands at 670 and 535 nm corresponding to Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>+ and Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ ions. The maximum quantum yield value of red luminescence is 47<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for glass-ceramics with 0.05 mol.% MnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Generating N00N-states of surface plasmon-polariton pairs in a nonlinear nanoparticle on metallic substrate
abstract: We study the generation of surface plasmon-polariton pairs with a gallium arsenide nanoparticle located at the silver-air interface. We demonstrate theoretically that N00N-states of surface plasmon-polariton pairs with N=2 can be obtained for certain excitation geometries. The effect can be physically interpreted as the result of a quantum interference between pairs of induced sources, each emitting either signal or idler plasmons.

articleTitle: High harmonics of an optical pump in presence of a strong terahertz field
abstract: We show that an arbitrary weak optical pulse acting together with a strong almost ionizing terahertz few cycle pulse allows efficient generation of harmonics of the optical field. The harmonics merge into a broad continuum if the optical pulse contains just a few field oscillations

articleTitle: Effective charge transfer within 2D layered nanostructures of PbSe-MoS2 colloidal nanoplatelets
abstract: We report the creation of layered 2D PbSe-MoS2 nanostructures which demostrate efficient electron transfer from PbSe nanoplatelet to MoS2 nanoplatelet. Charge transfer was confirmed by means of Results of the work show that ultrathin layers of transition metal dichalcogenides sensitized by 2D lead chalcogenide nanostructures can be effectively used in photodetectors with a spectral sensitivity extended to the near-IR range.

articleTitle: Scalar vortex generation using retrorefectors
abstract: An experimental study of a retroreflective spatial-polarization interferometer is presented in this article. A scalar optical vortex is generated using combination of a two cube-corner reflectors that have a special interference phase-shifting coating. Previously our team experimented with such interferometer, creating a vector vortex beam. In this experiment creation of a scalar vortex beam is considered.

articleTitle: Thallium halides based IR gradient crystals and optical fibers development
abstract: Using the solid-state diffusion method, gradient crystals of thallium halides were obtained with both an increasing refractive index to the center and a decreasing one, which corresponds to scattering and focusing lenses. Optical fiber extrusion was tested, experimental samples of gradient light guides made of thallium halides with a diameter of 1 mm were obtained.

articleTitle: Resonant Scattering in Wurtzite Semiconductors
abstract: The Raman scattering of light under excitation near the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{n}=2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{n}=1}$</tex> exciton levels in ZnS and the hyper-Raman scattering near two-photon resonance with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{n}=2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{n}=2}$</tex> exciton levels in ZnO were theoretically investigated, taking into account the influence of the complex top valence band.

articleTitle: Multi MeV high charge electron beam source utilizing 1 TW laser and shock wave in gas jet target
abstract: The high charge electron beam is generated at interaction of 1 TW laser pulse with gas target tailored by nanosecond prepulse forming a shock wave. Propagation of intense femtosecond pulse through complex plasma slab accelerates electrons up to 10 MeV. The debris free target has potential to kHz laser application and electrons energy enhancement using more powerful femtosecond laser pulse.

articleTitle: Optical frequency comb in optoelectronic oscillator with delay line and microresonator
abstract: We proposed and studied a new method which allows producing an optical frequency comb in an optoelectronic oscillator. In this method, comb parameters can be adjusted by controlling CW laser and microwave filter frequencies and amplitudes of modulating signals supplied to the arms of Mach-Zehnder modulator having two separate microwave inputs. Characteristics of the system were studied with numerical modeling for delay line and mictoresonator in the optoelectronic oscillator loop.

articleTitle: Raman spectroscopy for offshore hydrocarbon deposits detection
abstract: Since the raw material base replenishment is one of the priority economical tasks and the most promising oil and gas provinces are predicted in the Arctic region aquatic areas, which are characterized by high vulnerability, it is necessary to develop new environmental monitoring methods for marine deposits detection. For this purpose, the use of Raman remote monitoring system is proposed. The results of using Raman spectroscopy for indicators substances detecting are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Laser osteoperforation in the treatment of the distal tibia osteomyelitis
abstract: Currently, the treatment of distal tibia osteomyelitis remains a hot topic for discussion. Nowadays, the search for an optimal treatment method is relevant. The traditional method involves radical segmental bone resection to the level of healthy tissue, which in turn leads to bone defect, which significantly increases treatment and rehabilitation time

articleTitle: Parametric gain in the fiber with periodically varying dispersion
abstract: Modulation instability in the fibre with dispersion modulation and associated parametric amplification is investigated. It has been confirmed that in such fibers modulation instability is observed even in the case of positive dispersion. The prospect of using the fiber with large nonlinearity and periodic dispersion for parametric amplification with an expanded gain band due to parametric resonances is shown.

articleTitle: Optical spectroscopy of the Er3+ ion in BaY2F8 crystal and YSAG ceramics
abstract: We report about luminescent properties of yttrium scandium aluminum garnet (Er: YSAG) ceramics and fluoride crystal BaY<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>: Er.

articleTitle: The concept of multimodal prevention and treatment of new coronavirus infection COVID-19 by drug photosensitizers and photodynamic therapy on their basis
abstract: A study of antiviral low-dose photodynamic therapy with pharmacopoeia photosensitizers in the form of methylene blue and chloride E6 (Radachlorin) solutions in vitro demonstrated complete inactivation of SARS-CoV-2 in suspension and protection of Vero E6 cells even 3.5 hours after their infection with coronavirus at concentrations of photosensitizers 100–1000 times lower than the recommended pharmacopoeia forms of these drugs.

articleTitle: Rate and degree of platelets aggregation in cardiovascular diseases: studies by light scattering technique
abstract: The aim of this work was to measure parameters of platelet aggregation in patients with arterial hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus using light scattering technique. The degree and rate of platelets aggregation in patients with these diseases are increased compared to those in healthy people.

articleTitle: AlGaInN LED Pump System for Ti:Sapphire Lasers
abstract: High-power AlGaInN LEDs are of interest for pumping of Ti-sapphire lasers. In this regard, comprehensive studies of the power and spectral’ characteristics of LEDs in short-pulse modes used to laser pump were carried out. The energy capabilities and spectral properties of LED excitation of Ti-Sapphire were revealed. Designs of LED arrays and a laser head have been developed, the distribution of pumping in the active element have been simulated.

articleTitle: Two-wavelength holography applications for additive manufacturing
abstract: The experimental setup, based on a two-wavelength holography method is described. The possibility of recognizing defects of the order of 25 μm are demostrated. The ability of pulsed two- wavelength holography with 0 new inexpensive laser source is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Nanosecond Nd:glass Laser with Variable Radiation Coherence of “Kanal-2” Facility
abstract: A multimode neodymium glass laser with the possibility of varying spatial and temporal coherence is discussed. Its resonator is designed in such a way to generate close to the maximum number of transverse and longitudinal modes. Such type of radiation enables to improve the homogeneity of target irradiation and reduce the negative factors impact significantly.

articleTitle: Optical Methods for Controlling the CaSO4·2H2O Crystallization Process in the Presence of a Seed
abstract: To elucidate crystallization mechanism of CaSO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>.2H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O the characteristics of a dispersed impurity in water of various degrees of purification and initial solutions prepared on its basis were determined (Table 1).

articleTitle: Quantum Engineering of Bright-Dark Optical States of Resonantly Interacting Rare Earth Ions with Nanolocal Stark Effect
abstract: Earlier an idea to use controlled with modern Scanning Probe Microscopy (SPM) technique resonant interaction of dipoles (fluorescent rare earth (RE) ions in crystals) was put forward. Here we discuss the possibility to exploit nanolocal Stark effect, caused in such systems by strong inhomogeneous electric fields of sharp SPM electrodes (tips), to engineer the dark - bright states of resonantly interacting dipoles: their energies and decay (decoherence) rates can be strongly influenced by such fields.

articleTitle: Interferometry and spectroscopy of Cr3+:LiCaAlF6 crystals for tunable wavelength laser sources
abstract: Here we report on physical, spectral and gain characteristics of crystals for near IR active medium Cr:LiCaAlF6 grown by Bridgeman method. Samples have shown good homogeneity of refractive index and high optical quality. Optical spectroscopy characteristics together with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cr}^{3+}$</tex> content distribution have been investigated, as well as experiments on light amplification and laser oscillation have been performed.

Author Keywords: lasers of near IR spectral range

articleTitle: Ga2O3 and GaN nanoparticles synthesis by femtosecond laser ablation in ammonia environment
abstract: In the present work beta-gallium oxide and gallium nitride nanoparticles have been synthesized on the silicon wafer surface by femtosecond pulsed laser ablation of a metallic gallium target in ammonia vapor environment of various concentrations under the action of an electrostatic field.

articleTitle: Pulsed inductive Ne I laser
abstract: Lasing on 3p-3s transitions of neutral neon atoms upon pumping neon and its mixtures by a pulsed inductive discharge was obtained. The emission spectrum, depending on the pumping conditions, consisted of individual lines with wavelengths of 540.1,585.3, and 614.3 (594.4) nm.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of dynamic coherent beam combining in turbulent atmosphere with taking into account the double-pass delay
abstract: Numerical investigation of dynamic coherent beam combining of 7-channel laser radiation and its focusing on the remote target in turbulent medium has been carried out using the stochastic parallel gradient algorithm with the double-pass delay taken into account. Beam combining efficiency has been explored under various ratios between the phasing system frequency and Greenwood frequency.

articleTitle: Investigation of the effect of laser-induced plasma parameters on surface heating
abstract: In this work, we studied the heating of an AISI 304 wafer in the laser-plasma femtosecond ablation mode. The results of measuring the temperature of heating of the sample surface under the action of laser radiation in the point mode of exposure to laser radiation and in scanning with a beam at a constant number of acting pulses are presenting.

articleTitle: Localized and enhanced photodynamic processes through microsphere-assisted microscopy
abstract: The principal aim of this work is to give a perspective on the use of a single dielectric microsphere to control light focusing and collection from a substrate, also operating with short laser pulses. The possible advantages in the selective enhancement of surface photodynamic and thermo-mechanical processes on various kinds of substrates are discussed, especially in the presence of thin films or biological molecules.

articleTitle: The use of dielectric nanoparticles doped with rare-earth ions to increase the thermal effect of laser radiation of various wavelengths on biological tissues
abstract: The paper presents the results of in-vivo experiments on the non-contact effect of laser radiation with different wavelengths on the skin of animals (rats) pre-coated with nanoparticles doped with rare-earth ions (Ho<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>, Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>, Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>, Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>). We carried out a comparative assessment of the degree of damage to biological tissues after non-contact exposure to laser radiation with and without preliminary coating with nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Generation of a frequency comb with a gain-switched laser in a self-injection locking regime
abstract: Optical frequency combs provide unique opportunities for many practical applications and cutting-edge technologies. Hereby we demonstrate experimentally a generation of a frequency comb in visible range at 638 nm with a Fabry-Perot laser diode in a gain-switched regime and self-injection locked to a whispering gallery mode microresonator.

articleTitle: Room temperature Ce-doped chalcogenide glass laser
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a Ce-doped chalco-genide glass laser pumped by a Fe:ZnSe pulsed laser at room tem-perature. The laser performance of the Ce-doped active element under different pump wavelengths is realized and compared. The thermal effects that occurred in the Ce-doped active element are discussed.

articleTitle: Distributed Random Reflectors Inscribed in a Single-Mode Optical Fiber with Femtosecond Laser Pulses
abstract: We present experimental results on direct femtosecond pulse inscription of different-type random reflectors in single-mode optical fibers. In particular, we compare the backscattering efficiency of randomly chirped fiber Bragg gratings, multipoint Fresnel reflectors, and continuous Rayleigh/Mie reflectors.

articleTitle: KDP crystal is a medium for temporal self-compression of high-energy near IR femtosecond pulses
abstract: KDP crystal can be used for simultaneous spectrum broadening and temporal self-compression of near infrared femtosecond laser pulses with high peak power. It is analyzed a possibility of using KDP crystal for temporal self-compression. An impact of third order dispersion of KDP crystal to pulse shortening and peak power increase at standard post-compression technique is analyzed for peak intensities ∼TW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of morphology and physical properties of chitosan-gelatin nanofibers by coaxial electrospinning
abstract: In this work, chitosan and gelatin solutions were subjected to coaxial electrospinning. Using statistical analysis of scanning electron microscopy data, the formation of core-shell nanofibers with an average diameter from 79 to 90 nm was shown. The study of the stability of electrospinning showed the stabilization of the process with an increase in the content of acetic acid in the gelatin solution. According to the analysis of the mechanical properties of nanofiber materials, a twofold increase in the Young's modulus was revealed with an increase in the content of acetic acid from 50 to 90 vol.%.

articleTitle: IR laser generation based on atomic transitions of cesium and rubidium when pumping to high-located levels
abstract: We obtain laser generation on cesium and rubidium atoms at wavelengths in the range of 2 – 5.5 µm when pumping to high-located levels (7P - IOP for cesium atoms and 6P – 8P for rubidium atoms). The pumping conversion efficiency into lasing energy is investigated.

articleTitle: Raman spectroscopy of the interaction of carbon-coated iron nanoparticles with proteins
abstract: In this work, using Raman spectroscopy, the interaction of graphene-coated iron nanoparticles (G-Fe NPs) with the proteins lysozyme and immunoglobulin G (IgG) is studied. Two additional peaks in the Raman spectrum in the region of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$655-730\ \text{cm}^{-1}$</tex> reflecting the interaction of G-Fe NPs with IgG were found for their solution. The amplitude of the found peaks decreases significantly with a change in pH to 4, which is below the isoelectric point of the IgG. In the spectrum of solution of G-Fe NPs and lysozyme, at pH values below the lysozyme isoelectric point, no additional peaks reflecting the interaction of nanoparticles with protein were observed.

articleTitle: The effect of laser radiation on the BSA conformation
abstract: The effect of laser radiation on the buffer solution of bovine serum albumin (BSA) was studied. In this work, we irradiate aqueous solutions of BSA with a 532 nm laser source with pulse energy 70 μJ and pulse duration 10ns. It has been shown there is a change in the secondary structure of the protein

articleTitle: Fluorescence lifetime measurements for kidney ischemia monitoring in minimally invasive surgery
abstract: The paper demonstrates the results of the application of fluorescent and diffuse reflectance measurements in laparoscopic renal surgeries during the warm ischemia. The experimental setup and results of the combined use of optical modalities for cellular metabolism and tissue saturation assessment are described.

articleTitle: Optimized production of charged particles and thermonuclear neutrons from large nanoclusters irradiated with a relativistically intense ultrashort laser pulse
abstract: The interaction of ultrashort laser pulses of subrel-ativistic intensity with large nanoclusters is studied. The cluster target parameters were optimized based on 3D particle-in-cell simulations (PIC) to find a laser plasma regime that maximizes the number of high-energy deuterons and fusion neutrons. The considered design of the laser target has the potential to be used in a compact short laser driven source of neutrons.

Author Keywords: compact laser based DD neutron source

articleTitle: Fabrication of hydrophobic surfaces of aluminum alloys by laser irradiation
abstract: Laser modification of aluminum alloys with inclusions of B4C microparticles is of significant interest due to a significant increase in strength and temperature characteristics of the obtained material. In the process of laser irradiation of a composite material with an aluminum matrix, it is possible to form cluster objects that change the density of alloying additives distribution on the surface. In this work, we propose the creation of hydrophobic surfaces with macrogeometry controlled by the laser beam trajectory, and microgeometry determined by the target surface modification processes during local laser heating

articleTitle: Spatial chirp of the collimated single-cycle THz pulse
abstract: In this work the results of simulation of single- and multi-cycle pulse collimation are shown. Spatial and temporal field distribution of single-cycle pulse, which is typical for instance for THz radiation, were compared with the field distribution of multi-cycle pulse under the same conditions. Spatial chirp was observed for a single-cycle pulse - on-axis spectrum of the collimated single-cycle pulse is blue-shifted in comparison with the initial spectrum of the quasi-point source, whereas the off-axis spectrum is narrower and red-shifted.

articleTitle: Performance study of acousto-optic deflectors for femtosecond laser pulses
abstract: Theoretical and experimental analysis of angular chirp at the output of an acousto-optic deflector (AOD) is performed. Theoretical AOD dispersion model is developed and experimentally accessed for a paratellurite AOD operating with broadband femtosecond laser pulses at 800 nm. Optimization strategy for AOD design aimed at femtosecond laser radiation is discussed in the report.

articleTitle: Determination of Refractive Indices of the AgBr - AgI System Crystals in the Infrared Range
abstract: This work is devoted to the determination of the refractive index of crystals with a composition from 0 to 36 mol. %AgI in AgBr. For measurements, we used polycrystalline plates based on the single crystals with a composition 3, 13, 25 and 36 mol. % AgI in AgBr. The samples refractive indices were determined by the spectroscopic method in the wavelength range from 3.0 to 14.0 µm.

articleTitle: Biodegradable containers for drug delivery to tumours
abstract: To mitigate the hindered transport of multifunctional diagnostics and therapeutics nanoagents in the tumour tissue, we introduce a new drug delivery concept, which relies on drug container passive accumulation in the tumour vasculature followed by a rapid release of small-molecule payload that penetrates through capillary walls to the tumour interstitium and results in deep penetration in the tumour.

articleTitle: Infrared laser imaging based on up-conversion luminescence of SrF2:RE (RE = Er, Tm, Yb, Ho)
abstract: At the present time, infrared laser imaging based on up-conversion luminescence is used in different applications. These include bioimaging, biomedicine, infrared microscopy, detection of pollutions and greenhouse gases, solar energy etc. Thereby, in the present paper, we investigated the up-conversion luminescence (UCL) of fluoride phosphors. Fluorite-type SrF2:RE (RE = Er, Tm, Yb, Ho) phosphors were synthesized by co-precipitation from an aqueous nitrate solution technique. Upon laser excitation at 1532, 1645 and 1940 nm UCL of SrF2:RE (RE = Er, Tm, Yb, Ho) phosphors in the visible and near-infrared spectral region were recorded. The rare-earth concentration ions dependence of UCL intensity was studied. Also, we estimated the UCL energy yield in the visible and near-infrared spectral range. Calculated chromaticity coordinates and color temperatures showed that SrF2:RE (RE = Er, Tm, Yb, Ho) phosphors are characterized by the yellow-green and red-orange UCL. The application of up-conversion phosphors for visualization of near-infrared laser radiation is discussed.

articleTitle: Diffractive holographic elements for solar energy
abstract: The possibility of using various types of holographic structured elements as diffractive deflectors for solar energy is considered and the conditions for the expansion of the angular range corresponding to the high diffraction efficiency are determined. The efficiency of elements use is assessed taking into account the trajectory of the Sun.

articleTitle: Fe2+:ZnAl2O4-Based Transparent Glass-Ceramics: Tailoring Iron Absorption at $\sim 2\ \mu \mathrm{m}$
abstract: Transparent glass-ceramics of the zinc aluminosilicate system based on Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+-doped ZnAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> gahnite nanosized (5–16 nm) crystals are developed in different redox conditions. Their structure and spectroscopic properties are studied. The glass-ceramics are promising as saturable absorbers for lasers operating at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Functional hybrid structures based on porphyrins and gold nanoparticles for optical sensors
abstract: The mechanisms of interaction between optically excited porphyrins and gold nanoparticles determine the functional properties of hybrid structures based on them and make it possible to create various optical sensors. The mechanisms of charge and energy transfer, luminescence quenching and the temperature dependence of the luminescence intensity have been studied.

articleTitle: Infrared radiation transfer simulation of a two-layer bio-tissue based on the Bethe-Salpeter equation
abstract: Light scattering methods are currently actively used to study biological tissues, primarily for medical applications. An important area is the rapid field diagnosis of various brain injuries. We present results of numerical simulations of the infrared radiation backscattering from a layered biological tissue, primarily from the “skull-brain” system. The Monte Carlo simulations are based on the Bethe-Salpeter equation. We modified the standard procedure for detecting backscattered photons, which led to a significant reduction in the computation time.

articleTitle: Oxidation of biopterins under exposure to UV light from LED
abstract: Here we report the study of processes of tetrahydrobiopterin oxidation upon irradiation with UV light form LED source. We have detected the dihydropterin dimers formation initiated by UV light.

articleTitle: Light Interaction with Individual Impurity Atoms in a Waveguide
abstract: We study the interaction of quasi-resonant light with point impurity atoms embedded into transparent solid dielectric in a waveguide focusing our attention on the case when interatomic separations are much larger that the wavelength of light. We demonstrate the effect of incomplete spontaneous decay of a single excited atom in a waveguide and extremely long-range dipole-dipole interaction between different atoms.

articleTitle: Optical limiting properties of low-symmetry magnesium phthalocyanine complex bearing a pentachlorocyclotriphosphazene moiety
abstract: Phthalocyanines (Pc) are represented as the conjugated electronic system that can be readily affected by simple chemical reactions to create effective optical limiters. This work demonstrates the result of the interaction of nanosecond laser radiation (16 ns) at the second harmonic wavelength of 532 nm with the solution of asymmetrically substituted magnesium phthalocyanine complex (ppz- Pc<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sup>Mg), containing one pentachlorocyclotriphosphazene fragment at the periphery, in the tetrahydrofuran (THF).

articleTitle: High-purity GaxGe40-xS60 and GaxSb40-xS60 glasses as promising materials for laser optics
abstract: New method for preparation high-purity Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40-x</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf> and Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40-x</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf> glasses with a low content of hydrogen, oxygen impurities and heterogeneous inclusions have been developed. A comprehensive study of the glasses properties has been carried out. The optimal compositions of glasses for use in fiber optics have been determined.

articleTitle: Anion Exchange in Yb-Doped All-Inorganic Perovskite NCs
abstract: Perovskite nanocrystals have demonstrated an excellent possibility of tuning their optical properties in the visible and near-infrared ranges (NIR).
