At present, Yb-doped perovskites CsPbCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>are popular optical nanomaterials for the development of the next-generation electronic devices due to the sharp electronic transition of ytterbium in the NIR. Here, we have developed anion exchange procedures with usage of different chemical compounds and studied optical properties in visible and near-infrared ranges of obtained nanocrystals.

articleTitle: Effect of ultrasonic treatment for oxide ceramics preparation with improved luminescent properties
abstract: In the present work, treatment by intense ultrasonic was used during dry pressing of an YSZ and YAG:Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ nano- and micro- powder. The effect of the ultrasonic treatment on the structural and luminescent performances of oxide ceramics obtained by conventional sintering of the pressed compacts was studied.

articleTitle: Ultrashort Pulses Amplification In Er-Yb Composite Fiber
abstract: A comparison of ultrashort pulses with a central radiation wavelength of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.53\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> amplification in standard silica-based and composite active fibers was made. We have shown that pulse shape distortion in a composite fiber with Er/Yb co-doped phosphate glass core and silica cladding occurs at large values of the signal gain coefficient.

articleTitle: Thermal effect of femtosecond laser pulses in terms of laser-assisted hatching procedure on mammalian embryos
abstract: An assessment of thermal effect of femtosecond laser pulses during microsurgical procedures on embryos is performed. Issues of nonlinear absorption of laser pulses in aqueous medium are of crucial significance, as well as issues of subsequent heat transfer. Temperature evolution in the center of focused laser beam is presented from femtosecond to millisecond time scales.

articleTitle: Formation of low-cycle femtosecond pulses from radiation of a sub-ps ytterbium laser
abstract: A laser system has been developed for generating low-cycle femtosecond pulses with a central wavelength of 910 nm (or 2100 nm), a duration of several field oscillations with a kilohertz pulse repetition rate. The main advantage of the original approach is the optical synchronization of fs pulses with pump laser radiation.

articleTitle: Development and optimization of integrated photonic waveguide and passive devices on silicon on lithium niobate material platform towards creation of phase modulator
abstract: The numerical design procedure for the special type of waveguide, its parameters, and based on this waveguide directional and MMI coupler is discussed. We focus on the waveguide dimensions optimization for the phase modulator which appeared to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${90\mathrm{x}900}$</tex> nm for efficient modulation. The minimum bending radius, minimal distances between waveguides, and directional and MMI -coupler topology were obtained.

articleTitle: Yb:YAG chirped-pulse amplifier with passive coherent combining
abstract: Passive coherent combining for the two-channel Yb:YAG chirped-pulse amplifier is successfully implemented that allowed doubling output pulse energy in comparison with a single amplifier limited by the optical breakdown. 10mJ pulse energy at 1.5 kHz repetition rate and 5mJ at 6kHz is demonstrated together with high gain coefficient and perfect beam quality.

articleTitle: Experimental facility to study the possibility of laser action at the p-s transition of noble gas atom under excitation by 6Li(n,α)3H nuclear reaction products
abstract: The most promising are lasers based on infrared d-p transitions of noble gases. It is promising to create a laser based on 2p-1s transitions of noble gases in shorter wavelength region, with higher quantum efficiency. It is necessary to solve deactivation problem of lower 1s-level, two of these levels are metastable, two are resonant, radiation is trapped on them. Lithium serves as a source of laser mixture pumping with products of 6Li(n,a)3H nuclear reaction, also effectively deactivates lower 1s-levels. The work describes experimental facility to study the possibility of laser action under gas mixtures excitation by 6Li(n,a)3H nuclear reaction products in the pulsed nuclear reactor core.

articleTitle: Airflow turbulence testing by decomposition of the wavefront of probing laser radiation by Zernike polynomials
abstract: The results of experiments on probing the thermal airflow by laser radiation are presented. The wavefront was measured using a Shack-Hartmann sensor. One of the main requirements for the sensor during such measurements is the frequency of its operation. The frequency of 2000 Hz was used in the experiments, which made it possible to record the frequency of turbulence changes at least 200 Hz. To obtain statistical information, a sample of coordinates offset of the focal spots of the sensor was recorded. The reconstruction of the laser radiation wavefront was carried out using Zernike polynomials. As a result, a transition was made from a sample of offset coordinates of focal spots to a sample containing coefficients of expansion by Zernike polynomials. Statistical processing of the sample using the Fourier transform made it possible to determine the bandwidth occupied by each polynomial, as well as the amplitude of individual aberrations. It is shown that the calculations performed generally correspond to one of the consequences of the Taylor hypothesis - low-order aberrations are slower, but stronger compared to high-order aberrations. A graph is presented that allows us to evaluate the quality of correction of the laser radiation wavefront in the case of compensation of the first N Zernike polynomials.

articleTitle: Syncronous generation of nanosecond pulses at 1064 nm and 1240 nm in all-fiber laser
abstract: Generation of two synchronized pulses with broadly different wavelengths in the same fiber laser cavity opens up promising possibilities of entering the mid-IR wavelength range by difference frequency generation (DFG). One of the ways to generate synchronous pulses with very different wavelengths is Raman conversion in a P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>-doped fiber incorporated into the laser cavity in addition to an Yb-doped fiber. This work demonstrates, for the first time, efficient generation of synchronized pulses at wavelengths of 1064 and 1240 nm in such an all-fiber nested-cavity laser. An external DFG stage allows conversion of the laser output into pulsed radiation at ~7.5 µm.

articleTitle: Colloidal stability and oxidation of shungite carbon nanoparticles in aqueous dispersion mediated by fatty acid
abstract: The effect of linoleic acid on the structural features and resistance to aggregation of Shungite carbon nanoparticles in aqueous dispersion was studied using methods of dynamic light scattering and Uv-vis spectroscopy. This interaction has an important biological significance in the redox effects of nanoparticles in the presence of protein

articleTitle: Monitoring of alloying components burnout during laser powder cladding by laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy
abstract: The paper describes the application of the Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy method for monitoring the burnout of alloying elements during laser powder cladding. The diagram of the installation for this diagnosis is presented. The features of the process of obtaining a spectral signal suitable for analysis are described.

articleTitle: Hybrid nanostructures based on InGaN nanowires with deposited Ag NPs-SiOx for visible emission range
abstract: InGaN nanowires were synthesized by molecular beam epitaxy. The colloidal method was used to synthesize silver NPs coated with SiOx layers of different thicknesses. The dependence of the PL response of the InGaN-Ag-SiOx hybrid structure on the thickness of the SiOx layer has been studied for the first time.

articleTitle: Analysis of cells' response to photodynamic treatment with Radachlorin and PpIX by holographic techniques
abstract: Digital holographic microscopy and tomography were applied for analysis of morphological changes of cells caused by photodynamic treatment. Holographic techniques allowed for noninvasive long-time monitoring of living cells and provided quantitative data on the dynamics of cellular parameters. The experimental analysis performed provided data on cellular response to treatment for three established cell lines (HeLa, A549 and 3T3) and those developed from surgical material of individual patients with malignant tumors of different localizations.

articleTitle: The Comparison of OFC Generation Techniques for Fiber Optical WDM Networks
abstract: The improvement of globally deployed wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) network capabilities have received significant attention due to the rapidly growing demand for higher data rates and seamless connection to the Internet today. One of the most promising solutions to improve the spectral and power efficiency of these networks is to substitute laser arrays with optical frequency comb (OFC) generators. This article reviews and compares three perspective OFC technologies for channel carrier generation in telecommunication applications.

Author Keywords: highly nonlinear optical fiber (HNLF) whispering gallery mode resonator (WGMR)

articleTitle: Thick Cu Cylinder CAP Welding with Fiber Laser Under High Vacuum Conditions
abstract: We experimentally developed laser vacuum welding for Cu thick cylinder by using >2kW at 1080nm wavelength fiber laser. The welding condition is under 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> Torr, high vacuum condition to eliminate the oxidation of Cu seam welding parts as well as the fewer spatters during welding process. Under the high vacuum condition, the less energy is required compared with normal welding atmosphere to get the seam welding of the high heat transferred materials. Especially, in the experiments, we development both less adhesion of deposited materials on laser window and reusable the laser window after cleaning method against the contamination by spatters and plume during laser processing.

articleTitle: Photodiagnostics and Photodynamic Treatment of Glioblastoma Stem Cells with Porphyrins and Phthalocyanines
abstract: Investigations into efficacy and mechanisms of impact in photodynamic treatment (PDT) with different photosensitizers, based on porphyrins and phthalocyanines, on stem cells cultures isolated from human glioblastoma were carried out.

articleTitle: Optimization of Au-based nanoparticle-beacon system for biomedical applications
abstract: The discovery and application of new smart nanomaterials are one of the key goals of biomedicine. Here, we explored new sensing oligos for a recently developed nanoparticle-beacon (NB) system, aiming to expand the set of NB that could be used to detect several clinically relevant targets in the format of lateral flow assay (LFA). We optimized the oligos design, as well as determined buffer conditions for improved LFA performance. Thus, we expanded the set of oligos exploited as sensors in the NB and applied them in different assays.

articleTitle: Osmotically-induced strain in biological tissues during optical clearing: dependence on agent type and concentration
abstract: We apply phase-sensitive Optical Coherence Elastography (OCE) to evaluate and analyze spatially-resolved strain fields in porous biological tissues during their optical clearing. The study is focused on the first minutes of agent diffusion when equilibrium is not reached and concentration gradients as well as diffusion fronts are emerged with greatest intensity. The observed qualitative and quantitative parameters of the so-originated strain fields, such as strain sign and magnitude, the characteristic depth of its distribution, may shed light on fundamental mechanisms of the interstitial transport and mechanical response to osmotic stress. Particular examples of diffusion in cartilage, eye tissues and liver are considered.

articleTitle: Free carriers' dynamics in the bulk of silicon under mid-IR femtosecond laser excitation
abstract: Results of numerical simulation of free carriers' dynamics in the conduction band under femtosecond laser excitation in the mid-IR range (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.6\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>) in the bulk of silicon are presented. The electrons heating up to 8 eV which significantly exceeds the band gap is shown. The promotion of supercritical carrier concentration (8.5.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>) is demonstrated. These are critical to achieve the energy threshold (4.2 kJ/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) for melting silicon crystal lattice.

articleTitle: Optical properties of a hybrid films of J-aggregates and aluminum oxide formed on an island Ag film
abstract: The synthesis technique of nanoporous aluminum oxide on an island silver film has been developed. Such a structure was coated with J-aggregates and optical properties were studied for it. The transfer of optical excitation energy from oxygen vacancies of aluminum oxide to J-aggregates was observed.

articleTitle: High-energy Yb:YAG laser amplifier with near surface propagation of elliptical beam
abstract: It is proposed to use new laser active element scheme using elliptical beams propagate through an element of rectangular section along the only cooled side, differing from the thin slabs by higher efficiency of fabrication and mounting. 15 mJ pulse energy is achieved at the output of such amplifier at 1.5 kHz repetition rate limited by quality of the coatings.

Author Keywords: high average and peak power lasers

articleTitle: Fluid fraction spectroscopic analysis with artificial neural network
abstract: Downhole analyzer of fluid with spectrometer inside was used to obtain optical density spectral distributions for the different fluid compounds. We use fine optical density spectral distribution in 1600 - 1900 nm range with resolution of 1 nm to analyze the components of fluid. We use coarse optical density measurements in 1000–2100 nm range to correct the fine measurement. We use laser induced fluorescence as an additional channel. Ether, oil, water and solution were used to get the set of spectrograms to be analyzed by the artificial neural network. Convolutional neural network was used to analyze and classify 70% of the obtained spectrograms as a training set. The rest spectrograms were used as a test set, recognition accuracy was obtained about 98%. The same experiment results were demon-strated with using spectrograms from the other experiment, including emulsion, contaminated oil and water-oil emulsion. In the case of compound fluids, the detection result was depended on the components proportions. The spectrogram examples are presented, experiment results are also demonstrated, discussed and analyzed.

articleTitle: Generation of zepto-second scale hard X-ray pulses by Peta-Watt laser
abstract: In this report, we investigate the feasibility of generating multi-KeV photon pulses of several hundred zepto-seconds (zs) duration via all-optical setup, where PW laser produces multi GeV electron bunches, which create hard X-ray zs pulses in propagation through standard undulator/wiggler. We found the interaction regime when effective production of ultrashort (zs) hard X-ray pulses is possible, even though using a much longer driving laser pulse and electron bunch, with help of analytical modelling and numerical simulations by EPOCH and PUFFIN codes.

articleTitle: The Influence of Microenvironmental and Molecular Conformational Effects on Quantum Yield in NADH and FAD in Water-Alcohol Solutions
abstract: We studied quantum yield in biological coenzymes NADH and FAD in water-alcohol solutions. The analysis of the experimental results obtained allowed to separate the factors that influence on the fluorescence quenching in FAD and NADH: the role of molecular conformations in non-radiative relaxation processes in excited states, and solution viscosity and polarity.

articleTitle: Fluorochlorohafnate glasses with OH-groups reduced concentration doped by Tm3+, Er3+ - promising mid-IR laser medium
abstract: Fluorochlorohafnate glasses with different BaF 2/BaCl2 ratios in the glass batch were synthesized according to a developed technique for BaCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>purification through melt chlorination and a glass preparation procedure that considerably reduce the DB-groups concentration and chlorine vaporization rate. The fluorescence spectra and luminescence decay kinetics of Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ - and Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ -doped glasses have been studied.

articleTitle: Femtosecond high repetition rate fiber laser-driven plasma microfocus X-ray source for imaging applications
abstract: We present new approach to femtosecond laser-plasma microfocus X-ray source driven by low energy 0.1MHz rate ytterbium fiber laser interacted with metal target in ambient atmosphere environment. The results of the generation line X-ray with a flux more than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> photons/s in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\pi$</tex> for X-ray imaging applications are discussed.

articleTitle: Fe:ZnSe laser with pumping by a diode side-pumped Er:YAG laser
abstract: We demonstrate the performance of a Fe+<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>:ZnSe laser pumped by radiation of a diode side-pumped Er:YAG laser. The Fe: ZnSe laser produced 53 mJ of output energy at a pulse duration of 300 s and a central wavelength of 4.2 µm with a slope efficiency of 42% with respect to absorbed pump energy. We have reached 0.5 W of average power.

articleTitle: The spectral properties of Er3+/bismuth active centers co-doped germanate glasses
abstract: Erbium-doped bismuth-germanate glasses have been synthesized and their spectral characteristics have been studied. The contour of the absorption spectra in the region of 450– 550 nm is represented by the superposition of the bands of erbium and BACs. It was found that the addition of erbium does not destroy bismuth active centers, which in the future makes it possible to expand the range of NIR luminescence.

articleTitle: Spectral and kinetic characteristics of promising agents for combined PDT based on YF3-CeF3: Tb3+ nanoparticles conjugated with Radachlorin by means of polyvinylpyrrolidone
abstract: In this work, we studied the spectral and kinetic characteristics of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{YF}3-\text{CeF}3: \text{Tb}3+$</tex> (15 %) nanoparticles with Radachlorin and polyvinylpyrrolidone. Strong energy transfer from nanoparticles to Radachlrine is shown. To assess the toxicity, we conducted an MTT tests for A549 cells in the presence of nanoparticles with the Radachlorin.

articleTitle: Envelope control of chirped ns laser pulses with SLM-base shaper
abstract: A possibility of producing laser pulse shaping of infrared chirped pulses (1nm spectral width, 1 ns duration) is investigated. It is shown, that SLM-based shaper can be used for the pulse shape precompensation before an amplifier chain

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg grating interrogattion based on self-sweeping Yb-doped ring fiber laser
abstract: In this paper, we present a demonstration of the fiber Bragg grating (FBG) interrogation technique based on a self-sweeping Yb-doped ring fiber laser. The laser generates a sequence of single-frequency (with a line width of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.7 \ \text{MHz}$</tex>) rectangular pulses with quasi-CW intensity dynamics. The optical frequency of the laser changes sequentially from pulse to pulse by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10\ \text{MHz}$</tex>. An FBG spectrum is measured. It is comparable with spectrum obtained with a standard optical spectrum analyzer (OSA).

articleTitle: High-power Semiconductor $1.3-1.6\ \mu \mathrm{m}$ Laterally-Coupled Distributed Bragg Reflector Laser
abstract: The output characteristics of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.3-1.6\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> high-power single-frequency DFB-lasers with a laterally coupled Bragg diffraction grating were experimentally studied.

articleTitle: Laser microsurgery and fusion of multicellular spheroids for studying regeneration
abstract: Analysis of multicellular spheroids regeneration and fusion process was performed. The energy of laser pulses of microdissection for soft spheroids was less than for stiff, softer spheroids fused 1 day faster than stiff. Reparative processes after microdissection occurred gradually over seven days. Cell spheroids fusion is not entirely captured with the models based on the coalescence of liquid drops.

articleTitle: Raman and fluorescence lifetime imaging of cellular carotenoids distribution in algae
abstract: The results of the complex multimodal optical study utilizing Raman and fluorescence lifetime imaging of the cells of micro alga Bracteacoccus aggregatus BM5/15 are presented.

articleTitle: Underwater navigation: LiDAR sensing in water to 9 m distance through semi-transparent obstacles
abstract: A model experiment on LiDAR underwater navigation has been carried out. A 9-m-Iong tube filled with water was used as a model water medium. The laser beam of the compact LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging, 532 nm, ~2 ns, ~2 μJ/pulse, 4 kHz) was directed into the tube, and a non-transparent object (wall of the room) was sensed through the water. A unique LiDAR sensing technique based on a gated single-photon avalanche diode detector allowed successful detection of a non-transparent object through several scattering obstacles (up to three 1/2/3-layered plastic meshes). The possibilities of unmanned vehicles navigation and docking under water using LiDARs are discussed.

articleTitle: Modeling of Nanoparticles Formation Process due to Pulsed Laser Ablation in Liquids
abstract: In this work, we investigate the mechanism of NPs generation in liquids as a function of the pulse duration, the indecent fluence, and the irradiation regime (single-multi-pulse).

articleTitle: Phase-sensitive amplification in modulation instability sidebands
abstract: We consider the interaction of two intense pumps with the signal wave propagating in dispersion oscillating fiber. Oscillation of the fiber dispersion leads to the generation of multiple sidebands of the modulation instability. We found that the parametric amplification in the sidebands can be phase-sensitive. The parametric gain depends both on the phases of interacting waves and on the phase of dispersion oscillation. The parametric gain or anti-gain can be tuned in a wide frequency range using the phase of the oscillation of the fiber dispersion.

articleTitle: Weak Measurements with Adjustable Strength
abstract: The method for weak measurements with an ad-justable strength is proposed and implemented on an IBM quantum computer. The relationship between the strength, the qubit disturbance and the accuracy of the measurement are investigated.

articleTitle: Partially coherent conical refraction: Phase fluctuation and the Bessel-Gauss model
abstract: We derive a theory of the conical refraction for partially spatially coherent light, which is based on the phase fluctuation representation, and demonstrate non-diffractive propagation of the low-coherent conically refracted radiation in the far-field region.

articleTitle: Characteristics of bright betatron radiation from relativistic self-trapping of a short laser pulse in near-critical density plasma
abstract: We discuss the x-ray generation by electrons ac-celerated in the relativistic self-trapping regime of laser pulse propagation. It is shown that the secondary radiation has a high brightness. At the same time, this regime is accompanied by the particle interaction with a laser pulse that ensures partial polarization of synchrotron radiation and its nonisotropic angular distributions.

articleTitle: 0.6 J/ 3 ns 946 nm Nd:YAG laser
abstract: We developed a 946 nm Nd:YAG laser with output energy of 0.6 J/3 ns at pulse repetition rate of 50 Hz. The laser consists of single frequency laser diode, pulse slicer based on Pockels cell, high gain regenerative preamplifier and zero diffraction length ring cavity regenerative power amplifier with image rotation.

articleTitle: Nanostructure assisted laser desorption of Au+/Au-ions from gold surface below plasma threshold
abstract: The process of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Au}+$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Au}$</tex>-ions formation on a surface of nanostructured gold plate under pulsed laser irradiation with energy density below plasma threshold is studied. The role of nanoscale objects produced on the surface under laser irradiation higher than the plasma threshold in the ion formation process is discussed.

articleTitle: Phase and Chemical Transformations Kinetics in the Synthesis of a BaO-B2O3-Bi2O3 – (Y1-xErx)3Al5O12 Functional Glass-Ceramics
abstract: The kinetics chemical and phase transformations in the interaction of the glass-forming system BaO-B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> with (Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Er<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> in the glass-ceramics formation process were studied by DSC. The samples were characterized by powder x-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscope methods. The presence of devitrification according to DSC data proves that the samples synthesized in the temperature range 800-1300°C are glass-ceramic materials.

articleTitle: All-fiber Erbium-doped Ultrashort Pulse Laser with Switchable Generation Mode
abstract: We demonstrate the erbium-doped ultrashort pulse (USP) hybrid mode-locked fiber laser with 2 switch able generation modes - similariton-like pulses and dissipative soliton. The developed fiber laser generates femtosecond pulses with average power up to 7 mW at slightly positive net-cavity dispersion parameter ß2 with a repetition rate of 8,1 MHz.

articleTitle: Thermal properties of coupled-waveguide-based semiconductor lasers
abstract: We show experimentally how, utilizing coupled cavities, one can simultaneously improve the key parameters of diode lasers: internal optical loss and thermal resistance. Obtained results are promising for coming high-power semiconductor lasers.

articleTitle: High-power 4.5-µm Quantum Cascade Lasers with Two-Stage Epitaxial Growth
abstract: We study room-temperature performance of high-power mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers fabricated from the heterostructures grown by a combination of MBE and MOCVD epitaxial methods.

articleTitle: Nonlinear synthetic photonic lattices for optical neural networks
abstract: We reveal that a synthetic photonic lattice based on coupled waveguide loops can serve as a feed-forward neural network for processing of optical pulse sequences in time domain. We demonstrate the capabilities of the system in solving three different problems. We perform efficient training for dispersion compensation for the pulse train distorted in a linear fiber-optic link. We also show that the optical network with an intrinsic Kerr-type nonlinearity can perform a flexible nonlinear transformation of the pulse amplitude as well as discrimination of different pulse sequences.

articleTitle: Efficient approach for gain spectrum management of Bi-doped fibers
abstract: We present an efficient approach to manage the optical properties of Bi-doped P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> fibers by means of P content in the fiber core. Changing the concentration of P, we managed to vary the ratio between two types of bismuth active centers associated with Si and P and, as a result, significantly modify gain characteristics.

articleTitle: Reset-free stabilization of a fiber-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer using optical frequency shifters for low-noise microwave photonic links
abstract: A novel operating point stabilization method for fiber-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometers using optical frequency shifters is proposed. The method is capable of continuous reset-free compensation of an unbounded phase drift in arms of an interferometer with rates up to hundreds radians per millisecond.

articleTitle: Microresonators on surface of active fibers with active core for all-optical tuning
abstract: We present a mechanism of tuning a WGM microresonator formed on the surface of an active fiber by launching light into its core. We utilize this approach to create a feedback loop stabilizing the microcavity resonances.

articleTitle: Development of the alloyed quantum dots luminescence quenching based biosensor systems
abstract: Photoluminescent alloyed quantum dots are a promising material for biosensor development due to the high sensitivity of their optical properties to media conditions. Described sensing approaches based on quantum dots photoluminescence quenching. Discussed advantages and perspectives of alloyed quantum dots application.

articleTitle: Third harmonic generation in a medium with combined nonlinear response
abstract: We study the problem of third harmonic generation in a medium with combined quadratic and cubic nonlinear response under the condition of frequency doubling at big phase mismatching. Based on new analytical approach we found out the possibility of high frequency tripling conversion efficiency. This conclusion is supported by computer simulation results.

articleTitle: Local atraumatic fixation of the intestinal wall in the real-time artefact-free structural and angiographic transserous OCT imaging
abstract: We develop a method for atraumatic fixation of the intestinal wall with the aim to obtain real-time artefact-free structural and angiographic Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT and OCTA) images. A special cap was designed to be put on the end of the OCT probe, and connected to the medical suction pump to create a vacuum space. Testing of the vacuum cap on the wall of the small intestine of mini pigs allowed us to reduce the number of motion artifacts in OCT images compared to manual fixation from 84% to 8% and to obtain high-quality structural and angiographic OCT images in 92% of cases. We suggest that the new method of local atraumatic fixation of intestinal tissues may open up new possibilities for the use of OCT/OCTA in abdominal surgical interventions.

articleTitle: Pump and idler beams parameters dependence on pump power under conditions of mid-infrared difference frequency generation in PPLN
abstract: In this work, aspects of the spatial distribution of pump and idler beams was studied under conditions of a two-stage nonlinear conversion of high average power in a single periodically poled lithium niobate crystal (PPLN). A linearly polarized, 2-ns pulsed, dual-wavelength 1030 nm and 1560 nm fiber laser was used as a source for pump and signal radiation for difference frequency generation (DFG) process in PPLN. The mid-IR idler radiation near <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.0\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> wavelength was generated. Diameter and position of the idler beam waist at the converter output could be determined not only by diameter and position of pump waist but also by peak and average power of pump beam. This behavior could be explained by pump depletion effect and thermal lens appearance in the crystal. Significant change (up to 40%) in the diameter and position of the waists of the resulting pump and idler beam was experimentally observed depending on the pump radiation power in 5–50 W range. Such changes can be substantial for some applications and must be taken into account for the calculation of the matching optics at the output of the nonlinear optical converter.

articleTitle: Optical Antennas Interfaces Formation by Selective Femtosecond Laser Ablation
abstract: The paper proposes a technology for optical antennas interfaces formation using femtosecond laser radiation. An experimental scheme of the laser micromachining procedure is presented. The possibility of large-length thin-film microsized structures formation has been proved.

articleTitle: X-ray resonant reflectometry as a multifunctional synchrotron method for studying magnetic nanofilms
abstract: X-ray resonant magnetic reflectometry is a synchrotron based non-destructive method of investigation of electronic and magnetic depth profiles in nanoscale multilayers. The choice of x-ray photon energy close to the absorption edges makes the method selective to oxidation state, crystallographic environment and magnetization of individual chemical elements. The enhanced technique dealing with acquisition and modelling of the angle-energy maps of resonant reflectance is discussed in the present contribution.

articleTitle: Laser engineering of biological tissue and microbial systems
abstract: We presents the results related to developing laser additive technologies for use in regenerative medicine in tissue engineering and microbiology. The results of implementation of new approaches to form tissue engineering structures based on biocompatible and bioresorbable polymeric materials and the research results on the development of laser-induced bioprinting of living cells, cell aggregates, and microorganisms are presented.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of nonlinear photoionization of metal microparticles
abstract: The paper presents the model of a multiphoton ionization of micron-sized metal particles as a process of cascade transitions of electrons through a discrete system of energy levels

articleTitle: A Single-Scan PM-Fibers Polarization Axes Study
abstract: We propose optical scheme for single-pulse reflectometry of anisotropic optical fibers. In application with Brillouin analyzer this scheme was used for birefringence measurements of the Panda-type fiber. With phi-OTDR device, it allowed to increase a number of key parameters.

articleTitle: The influence of a local refractive index change on the splitting ratio of an integrated optical Y-branch on lithium niobate substrate
abstract: The power splitting ratio tuning of a lithium niobate integrated optical Y -branch caused by a local refractive index change was investigated. Controllable local refractive index change was produced by photorefractive effect at external laser irradiation. The dependences of the splitting ratio change on the position of the local refractive index change had interferometric nature. The effect could be used for precise tuning of the Y -branch splitting ratio.

Index Terms: Change In The Local Refractive Index

articleTitle: 2 um KYW:Tm,Ho laser with transverse diode pumping for passive Q-switching
abstract: The KYW:Tm,Ho laser operating at 2056 nm with 15 mJ and 25 ns pulse is used to study saturable absorption of PbS quantum-dot-doped silicate glasses. Various heat treatment conditions was used to prepare a series of saturable absorber samples having 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> exciton maximum around 2 um.

articleTitle: The influence of growth parameters of AlGaAs waveguide layers grown by MOCVD on the output characteristics of high-power laser diodes
abstract: The work presents the results of investigation into the influence of parameters of epitaxial growth of AlGaAs waveguide layers (temperature, gas mixture composition) on the output characteristics of laser diodes. Epitaxial growth modes have been considered at which minimum background concentration of holes in heterostructure waveguide layers is achieved. The dependencies of LD main characteristics on the concentration of holes in heterostructure waveguide layers have been calculated and experimentally studied.

articleTitle: Temperature stabilization of an Er:fiber-based femtosecond frequency comb
abstract: An effect of temperature changes in individual parts of a Er:fiber-based femtosecond frequency comb on the parameters of its offset frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{0}$</tex> is determined. A system for thermal stabilization of air inside the frequency comb has been implemented. As a result, temperature fluctuations inside the frequency comb decreased from ∼0.7°C to ∼0.1°C, inside the master Er:fiber laser - from 0.1 to 0.01 °C. This led to a significant decrease in the drift of the amplitude and frequency of the signal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{0}$</tex> in the free regime of operation (without stabilization the frequency comb to the frequency of the optical standard).

articleTitle: Numerical study of the plasma charge for the case of a cylindrical bunch irradiatedwith a laser pulse
abstract: A numerical simulation of a cylindrical plasma bunch with non-equilibrium ionic composition under the action of an external laser pulse is carried out. The pulse parameters are varied. An unsteady one-dimensional two-temperature radiation-hydrodynamic model is used. The model and its results are of interest for research in the field of active media formation of lasers in the extreme ultraviolet and soft X-ray ranges.

articleTitle: Effect of current localization on the output optical power in high-power laser-thyristors based on AlGaAs/GaAs/InGaAs heterostructures
abstract: The operation of a semiconductor laser-thyristor based on AlGaAs/GaAs/InGaAs heterostructures with a p-GaAs base thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.4\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> was under study. At the same supply voltage of 22 V, the drive current amplitude of 138 mA gives a more noticeable current localization near mesa-stripe edge in comparison with the case of the drive current of 1 mA.

articleTitle: Spectral approaches for depth analysis in diffuse optical diagnostics modalities
abstract: Strong dispersion of biotissue optical properties in visible and NIR ranges determines difference in probing depths in optical diagnostics modalities thus allowing to control probing depth by the choice of the wavelength range. The paper discusses spectral dependence of the probing depth and the accuracy of oxygen saturation reconstruction in diffuse reflectance spectroscopy and reviews dual-wavelength approach in fluorescence imaging.

articleTitle: Comparison of strain ultrasound elastography with compression optical coherence elastography for breast cancer characterization
abstract: The purpose of this study is to compare the results of ultrasound strain elastography (US-SE) with compression optical coherence elastography (C-OCE) measurements in breast cancer, using histologic analysis as the reference standard, and to assess factors that can affect the results of the two elastography techniques. We demonstrate that in comparison to US-SE, C-OCE have novel capabilities due to its ability to locally control pressure on the breast tissue and obtain local stress-strain curves. The obtained results confirm high potential of using C-OCE in intraoperative search for resection breast cancer margins.

articleTitle: Compact laser diode Lidar has opened new era an environmental sensing without eyes protection: To 100-anniversary of Nikolay Basov
abstract: In 1991 Russian scientist have opened the new era of an environmental sensing by eye-safe lidar. For the first time to our knowledge we have proposed the new lidar principles for environmental sensing by extreme low pulse energy when the probability of a return photon registration is <1. We have developed and tested the lidar with eye-safe energy density (<1 µJ cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>), We have used GaAlAs diode laser as transmitter and a gated SPAD as detector. The multilayers cloud's height and forest fires, forest biomass and agriculture plants were monitored by this lidar. It was involved in “Mars Polar Lander-99” mission as the first lidar to monitor of the Martian atmosphere. Actually that this new lidar's principle was used in the navigation system of unmanned cars and other vehicles and volcano Elbrus activity inside the tunnel above its chamber.

Author Keywords: eye-safe lidar operates on the new principles

articleTitle: Intence source of laser-produced unipolar terahertz pulses
abstract: A three-dimensional analytical solution for the near field for a terahertz unipolar pulse based on Maxwell's equations is shown. It is calculated in a transition sample in free space by a laser bunch of relativistic electrons as a result of radiation of a thin foil by a femtosecond laser pulse. The paper shows the theoretical obtaining of unipolar pulses from the Maxwell equations, as well as numerical simulations that confirm the theoretical conclusions. The temporal and spatial characteristics of the system are estimated, and the coefficient of conversion of laser radiation into unipolar terahertz radiation is also obtained.

articleTitle: An Increase in Luminescence Brightness of Nd3+: LaF3 Nanoparticles, Synthesized by Hydrothermal Microwave Method Promising for NIR Bioimaging
abstract: By transferring the initial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Nd}^{3+}:\text{LaF}_{3}$</tex> nanoparticles synthesized by hydrothermal microwave treatment, from aqueous colloidal solutions to DMSO, the possibility of increasing the luminescence brightness in the near IR spectral range is shown.

articleTitle: Formation of Low-Coherence Laser Beams in Dense Mixtures of Solid-State Microparticles and Liquids
abstract: Low-coherence lasers with intra-cavity diffusers based on slurry-like dense mixtures of crystal or glass microparticles and immersion liquids are proposed.

articleTitle: CW and Q-switch laser of ZrO2-Y2O3- Ho2O3 crystals
abstract: The energy and time characteristics of CW and Q-switched two-micron lasing at the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>→<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> transition of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>3+ ions in ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>o3-Ho2o3crystals under resonance pumping to the<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> level CW Tm:LiYF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> laser were investigated. The optimal parameters of the growth rate and thermal treatment of crystals, as well as the modes of mechanical and chemical-mechanical processing of the faces of active elements were revealed. Mechanisms for the occurrence of burns on the faces of active elements ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-Ho<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> at high laser energy densities have been proposed.

articleTitle: Analysis of hartmannogram images for scattered laser beam focusing by means of high-resolution stacked-actuator mirror
abstract: Recent researches in the field of laser beam propagation through the turbulent atmosphere and scattering aerosols showed the necessity of using adaptive optical devices to effectively control the phase and intensity distributions of the light. There are a big variety of the adaptive optical devices that can be used to solve the task mentioned above - deformable mirrors, spatial light modulators, etc. In this paper we demonstrate the use of the high-resolution stacked-actuator deformable mirror with 61 actuators on the round 60 mm aperture for focusing of a laser beam propagated through the relatively thick layer of a moderately scattering medium.

articleTitle: Cr2+:CdSe laser with moving active element
abstract: The thermal lenses limit the output power of the lasers on active Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+:CdSe element by ~1 W level, because the element possess adverse thermo-physical properties such as low thermal conductivity and high value of the thermo-optical coefficient. The transition from the classical scheme of construction of the laser source to the scheme with moving active element allowed to achieve more than 20 W with continuous wave Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+:CdSe laser.

articleTitle: Diode-Pumped 2128-nm Laser Based on Degenerate Intracavity OPO in KTP Crystal
abstract: Side-diode-pumped YAG:Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ laser with intracavity optical parametric oscillator in KTP crystal with collinear phase matching at wavelength of 2128 nm and slope efficiency of 2.5% was developed and tested as pump source for ZnSe:Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ laser.

articleTitle: Magneto-optical Faraday effect in polycrystalline ZnSe and Cr:ZnSe
abstract: The values of the Verdet constant at a wavelength of 632.8 nm in Cr: ZnSe and undoped ZnSe were obtained. It was shown that the Verdet constant in undoped zinc selenide does not depend on the crystallite size. The experimentally determined maximum value of the Verdet constant for Cr: ZnSe was 226.5 rad/(T·m), which is more than two times higher than the corresponding value for ZnSe.

articleTitle: Terahertz radiation sources and frequency converters based on topological insulators
abstract: Topological insulators made of bismuth chalcogenides are promising materials for sources and converters of terahertz radiation. The operation of a topological insulator nanofilm photoconductive antenna is demonstrated. The generation of the third and fifth harmonics of the terahertz frequency radiation in topological insulators of various chemical compositions is observed.

articleTitle: Development of optical vortices in a beam propagating in a turbulent atmosphere
abstract: Development of singular points in a coherent beam is considered in the paper. The initial phase of radiation was set by Zernike polynomials and by a random phase screen simulating atmospheric turbulence. Several methods of detection were used to register optical vortices.

articleTitle: Study of luminescence during sputtering of lithium in noble gas by a nanosecond electron beam
abstract: In experiments to study lithium sputtering in noble gas, a target with a deposited lithium layer is placed in the path of the electron beam. The lithium layer during bombardment by a pulsed fast electron beam is heated from 300 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{K}$</tex> up to 900 K. Analysis of obtained results allowed determining a temperature dependence of luminescence intensity, as well as promising mixtures of noble gases, atomic transitions for conducting in-pile experiments at a pulsed nuclear reactor. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathbf{p}_{6}\text{-}1_{\mathbf{S}4}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathbf{p}_{6}\text{-}1_{\mathbf{S}5}$</tex> transitions of xenon atom seems to be the most promising to create an inverse population.

articleTitle: On the scattering phase function of the infinitesimal scattering volume of turbid biological media
abstract: In the light transport theory, the scattering phase function (SPF) is commonly considered as independent on the absorption coefficient of a turbid medium. In this study for biological turbid media, we propose an approach to analytically derive SPF. It is shown that SPF for the infinitesimal scattering volume can depend on both scattering and absorption coefficient.

articleTitle: Using the steepness of the localized surface plasmon resonance phase response for highly sensitive detection of molecular binding events
abstract: This study demonstrated the capabilities of method which uses the steepness of the localized surface plasmon resonance phase response for sensing of molecular binding event.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of algorithms for centering the optical radiation image in the focal plane
abstract: In the problems of adaptive correction of distortions of radiation propagating in a turbulent atmosphere, as well as in problems of focusing laser radiation, the efficiency to a certain extent depends on the algorithm that estimates the radiation image in the plane of the receiving device. This paper presents the results of evaluating algorithms that determine the coordinates of the energy center of gravity of the focal spot within the recorded intensity distribution.

Author Keywords: image of optical radiation in the plane of the receiving device

articleTitle: OCT study of cataract simulation in the lens of a porcine eye
abstract: An OCT study of the laser-induced dynamics of the deformation response of the lens structure during cataract modeling using peroxide and formalin at two wavelengths is presented.

articleTitle: Using genetically engineered calcium indicator to identify the role of astrocytes in the development of Alzheimer's disease
abstract: A new calcium sensor has been developed to determine the functional activity of astrocytes in Alzheimer's disease an in vitro modeling

articleTitle: Integration of QKD in existing WDM optical networks: spectral methods of suppressing noise in the O-band
abstract: The performance of spectral filters and multiplexers that can be used for integrating QKD into existing DWDM networks are presented.

articleTitle: Autofocused asymmetric aberration laser beams
abstract: We have generated asymmetric aberration laser beams (aALBs) with auto-focusing properties. The asymmetry in the phase distribution of aALBs is deliberately exploited for controlling spatial intensity distribution, and thereby generating high-power densities, useful for several applications.

articleTitle: Engineering ultrashort pulses in infrared and upper terahertz bands using a laser pulse and a nanostructured target
abstract: Characteristics of infrared and upper terahertz bands radiation in three laser-target interaction modes are found with 2D numerical simulations. A superintense laser pulse extracts electron bunches with high charge from the target and accelerates them. During acceleration, the electron bunches produce high-power electromagnetic radiation. Choosing appropriate target nanostructure, the shape of the generated pulse can be engineered and a train of such pulses can be produced with a specified distance between them. It is shown that in multiterawatt laser systems, generated pulse amplitude can be on the subrelativistic level, while the conversion efficacy can be as high as one percent.

Author Keywords: interaction of laser radiation with matter
generation of terahertz and infrared radiation

articleTitle: Noncritical phase-matched THz generation in GUHP molecular crystal
abstract: A narrow-band coherent terahertz radiation source based on a semi-organic molecular crystal GUHP is presented. The unique resonant spectral features of the transmission in the terahertz frequency range make it possible to achieve the duration of generated THz pulses up to ~300 ps at a temperature of 10 K with a stable oscillation frequency of the electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: High fill-factor kW-level tunnel-coupled diode laser bar ($\lambda=910\ \text{nm}$) for 100-ns pulse sources
abstract: Pulsed 910 nm laser sources based on triple tunnel-coupled AlGaAs/InGaAs/GaAs heterostructures were developed and studied. High fill-factor (96%) microbars with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 800\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> aperture were fabricated and studied under pumping by high-current pulse source (up to 750A/130ns/1kHz). Peak optical power up to 1150W at 25°C and 905W at 75°C were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Role of optical feedback in formation of radiation properties of a Raman fiber laser with randomly distributed feedback well above generation threshold
abstract: Nonlinear effects are known to govern spectral properties of Raman fiber laser radiation well above the generation threshold, and the role of randomly distributed feedback in random fiber lasers is expected to be negligible. We numerically study spectral properties of a random fiber laser and a corresponding fiber amplifier with no feedback and emphasize the importance of Rayleigh backscattering.

articleTitle: Direct Femtosecond Laser Printing of Plasmonic Colors in Reflection at 25,000 DPI
abstract: Femtosecond-laser nanotexturing of the top metal films crowing a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) sandwich designed to support Fabry-Perot mode in the visible spectral range was carried out to realize multi-color printing of micro-scale structural color images at 25,000 dpi resolution. Applied pulse energy controls the resulting geometry of the surface modifications that vary from 3D nanojets to micro-holes affecting local surface reflectivity observed with an ordinary optical microscope in reflection mode.

articleTitle: Efficient generation and characterization of THz radiation in TW laser-plasma interaction
abstract: We had numerically and experimentally studied THz radiation generation in the interaction of a terawatt laser pulse with several dozens of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu m-\text{thick}$</tex> plastic tape target. Based on PIC simulations and measurements, the mechanism of THz radiation generation was found to be Coherent Transition Radiation (CTR). The proposed scheme can be relatively easily implemented on the kHz laser systems, resulting in a high-intensity high-flux THz radiation source.

articleTitle: Transverse Mode Structure of Mid-Infrared Quantum-Cascade Lasers: Experiment and Numerical Simulations
abstract: We study the evolution of the transverse mode structure of the high-power mid-infrared quantum-cascade lasers in the near- and far -field with an increase of pump current.

articleTitle: Down- conversion LiYF4:Tm3+, Yb3+ phosphors for optical temperature sensing
abstract: Down-conversion luminescence has been demonstrated in Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ - Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ co-doped LiYF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> upon the 688-nm excitation of Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>. For the sake of temperature sensing, luminescence decay time of Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ and luminescent intensity ratios were taken as temperature dependent parameters. The maximum sensitivities were 0.33 µs/K for LiYF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+(0,5%),Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+(60%) sample.

articleTitle: Kerr Comb Generation Efficiency in Microresonators and Optimal Pumping Regime
abstract: The increase of pump-to-comb conversion efficiency is a crucial problem for Kerr frequency comb generation in optical microresonators. We present a careful optimization of the setup parameters, such as pump power and coupling coefficient, for the best performance, showing the global maximum and discuss its attainability.

articleTitle: 1550-nm waveband VCSELs made by wafer-fusion technique
abstract: 1550-nm VCSELs with an active region of ten compressive-strained InGaAs QW, separated by the InP lattice-matched InAlGaAs barrier layers and GaAs/AlGaAs distributed Bragg reflectors are fabricated using wafer-fusion and molecular-beam epitaxy methods. Single-mode operation at output optical power of 4.8 mW, stationary and dynamic characteristics are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Characterization of perspective active medium based on mixed crystals Ce3+:LiCaxSr1-xAlF6
abstract: The aim of this work is describing the characteristics of promising active media based on mixed crystals <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ce}^{3+}:\text{LiCa}_{\mathrm{X}}\text{Sr}_{1-\mathrm{X}}\text{AlF}_{6}$</tex>. Optical studies of ions in the UV spectral range and the influence of various types of doping centers on laser characteristics in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ce}^{3+}:\text{LiCa}_{\mathrm{X}}\text{Sr}_{1-\mathrm{X}}\text{AlF}_{6}$</tex> mixed crystals will be also discussed.

articleTitle: Externally-Triggered Joule-Level Nanosecond Pulses Hybrid Laser Source
abstract: A fiber master oscillator and a multi-pass system of bulk amplifiers for generating an arbitrary laser pulse shape with an energy of up to 1 J were demonstrated. External triggering made it possible to obtain a pulse on demand.

articleTitle: Efficient Generation of Positrons in Laser Plasma for Measuring Super-High Laser Intensities
abstract: An electron in a strong electromagnetic field can emit a high-energy photon, which can subsequently decay into an electron-positron pair according to quantum electrodynamics (QED). The process of positron generation can take place only in the presence of very intense fields. In this study, we investigate the possibility of extracting super-high laser intensities by measuring the positron yield. Our numerical computations provide the total number of positrons as a function of the laser intensity for several different setups. In order to address the domain of super-high laser intensities, where an avalanche-like cascade process of pair production can appear, we design a recursive numerical procedure. It is shown that the laser intensity can be determined with a relative uncertainty of the order of ten percent in a wide range up to super-intense fields launching QED cascades.

articleTitle: Near-Ultraviolet Lasing in ZnO Microrod Ensemble
abstract: Near-UV whispering gallery lasing in ZnO microrod ensemble was observed. Low density of lasing microrods grown on side faces of the substrate made it possible to excite lasing in individual crystals. Study of as-grown crystals allowed us to avoid optical losses due to contact of crystals' lasing part with a substrate. Larger-diameter micro rods exhibited better lasing performance than smaller-diameter microrods.

articleTitle: Optical characterization of small-molecule-protein conjugates for development of express high-sensitive immunosensors based on magnetic biolabels
abstract: Currently, one of the most dangerous mycotoxin for humans and animals is ochratoxin A (OTA). Despite significant progress in modern approaches for detection of low molecular weight compounds, express methods for on-site sensitive quantification of OTA in food are still to be developed. Conjugates of OTA with a carrier protein - bovine serum albumin - were characterized in terms of kinetics of their interaction with monoclonal antibodies against OTA. Spectral interferometric methods were used for label-free characterization in a real-time mode. An express sensitive method was developed for on-site OTA detection in food based on the use of the characterized OTA-BSA conjugates combined with highly sensitive electronic registration of magnetic biolabels at combinatorial frequencies.

articleTitle: Quantum dots for control the concentrations of anthracycline antibiotics
abstract: Quantum dots (QDs) can be an optimal material for creating systems for determining the residual concentration of anthracycline antibiotics in blood, urine and tissues to optimize the dosage of chemotherapy drugs. The selection of the optimal composition of the structure and surface of QDs allows to achieve the best energy transfer and, as a result, the most reliable analytical system

articleTitle: Very low threshold InAs-based quantum cascade lasers
abstract: We present InAs-based quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) operating near 14 µm with a threshold current density as low as 630 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at room temperature, outperforming the best reported to date InP-based QCLs.

articleTitle: Laser Regime Analysis using Lyapunov Exponents
abstract: We use Lyapunov charts method for a single-mode, Raman, SBS and fiber lasers and fiber microcavities. Computed regime maps allow us to characterize spatio-temporal properties of established mode and predict the behavior of the electromag-netic field in the laser system, knowing how a specific instability in the cavity depends on the parameters of the given system.

articleTitle: Development and characterization of a label-free method for detection of folic acid
abstract: Rapid inexpensive tests with single-used consumables for determination of folic acid are highly demanded in medicine, as this substance is a vital component for production of healthy body cells, DNA replication, and formation of a spinal cord of the fetus at pregnancy. In this study, we propose and demonstrate a method of label-free detection of folic acid based on the spectral-correlation interferometry approach. The proposed method exhibits subnanomolar limit of detection and a wide dynamic range that covers clinically relevant concentrations of folic acid in humans.

articleTitle: Analysis of turn-on delay of quantum cascade lasers under pulsed pumping with linear front edge
abstract: We analyze turn-on delay of quantum cascade lasers under pulsed pumping with linear front edge. The analytical results are in a good qualitative agreement with numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Quantum Optics of Polyatomic Ensembles in a Waveguide
abstract: We study many-body cooperative effects in an ensemble of point impurity atoms located in a waveguide, such as single-photon superradiance, subradiance and light trapping. We show that in the case of single-mode waveguide, the time of radiation trapping exponentially increases with an increase of the size of atomic medium, which indicates the Anderson localization of light.

articleTitle: The interest of synchrotron x-ray microtomography for the study of defects in sapphire articles fabricated by bulk crystallization
abstract: We present a Synchrotron X-ray tomography investigation of sapphire crystals of a complicated shape. The concept of crystal shaping while the growth from the melt allows avoiding tooling and associated loss of material. However, the elimination of gas bubbles and dislocations remains a severe problem. In the present communication, we show and analyze the distributions of bubbles in sapphire tubes and ribbons grown with the Stepanov technique. We approve that microtomography implemented with Synchrotron Radiation using a conventional algorithm can give good results concerning the visualization of µm-sized bubbles.

articleTitle: Efficacy of photoactivated medicinal plant extracts
abstract: We present study on spectral-luminescent characteristics medicinal plant extracts, their ability to generate singlet oxygen upon photoexcitation and photodynamic effects of extracts on mammalian cell culture and different taxonomic groups of bacteria.

articleTitle: Sweeping range optimization in Er-doped self-sweeping fiber laser
abstract: We report here about self-sweeping range optimization in an erbium-doped fiber laser generating in the telecom L-band near 1603 nm. The cavity mirror reflection coefficient and the pump wavelength are varied during the optimization. The maximum scanning range obtained is 3.4 nm at the pump wavelength of 1548 nm and the mirror reflection coefficient of ∼ 36%.

articleTitle: Optimization of the optical scheme of weak absorption measurement in transparent materials
abstract: Comparative results of experimental studies and numerical analysis are presented using the developed original technique for simulating an installation for measuring ultralow absorption based on single-beam photothermal common path interferometry (PCI). The possibility of decrease the detection limit for volume absorption by the PCI method is shown to be significantly lower than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{-6}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$</tex>, absorption on the surface and in thin films is less than 1 ppm.

articleTitle: Laser Solitons with Phase and Polarization Singularities
abstract: We investigate, analytically and numerically, phase and polarization singularities of 2D-laser spatial solitons in a wide-aperture semiconductor laser with vertical cavity and saturable absorber. We present a wide family of such vector solitons characterizing the phase singularities by their integer topological charges for the two circular polarizations (the phase circulation divided by 2pi) and by semi-integer Poincare indices for polarization singularities (circulation of direction of the main axis of the ellipses divided by 2pi).

articleTitle: Laser based source of electrons/ions for nuclear medicine and nuclear waste transmutation
abstract: We presented the results of a comprehensive simulation of PIC-GEANT4 (particle-in-cell and Monte-Carlo) codes for the generation of high-energy electron or ion bunches by a short laser pulse and their application to assess the possibility of medical isotope production and nuclear waste transmutation.

articleTitle: Core-shell InGaN Nanowires: MBE Growth and Properties
abstract: The influence of the growth temperature on physical properties of InGaN nanowires grown by molecular beam epitaxy is considered. The growth conditions for synthesis of core-shell InGaN nanowires with a high In content are determined. The samples exhibit an intensive room temperature photoluminescence from green to orange spectral range.

articleTitle: Hybrid and integrated high-power pulse laser-thyristors
abstract: High-power hybrid semiconductor lasers - thyristors (λ = 900 - 920 nm) consisting of thyristor crystals soldered in series with an integrated semiconductor laser with one and three emitting sections are studied. The output characteristics of optimal source (hybrid laser-thyristor with three emitting sections) is P = 73 W, t= 6.4 ns, f = 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Phase edges detection in the presence of noise based on transport-of-intensity equation
abstract: A method for phase edges detection is presented. This approach allows to retrieve phase of a light wave from the intensity measurement in multiple planes using transport-of-intensity equation. Then edges detection implemented via ridding of noise-induced artefacts.

articleTitle: Measurement of laser radiation parameters by speckle interferometry
abstract: The article discusses the possibilities of simplified measurement of the key parameters of laser radiation on the basis of speckle interferometry and machine learning methods. It is demonstrated that the corresponding device may be designed as a compact and inexpensive laser accessory capable of replacing the entire conventional set of laboratory measurement equipment. Development of a new type of more universal accessory for characterisation of laser radiation will enable transition from the conventional concept ‘laser in the lab’ to the emerging advanced concept ‘lab in the laser’ allowing characterisation of output radiation without recourse to external specialised equipment.

articleTitle: Angular distribution of THz emission from cluster beam and electron dynamics in cluster plasma
abstract: In this work, we present and discuss experimental results of the angular power distribution of THz radiation from cluster jets that differ in cluster size and internal density of electrons in ionized clusters. The aim of the experiments was to verify the theoretical model of the mechanism of low-frequency generation in cluster plasma.

articleTitle: Bell-shaped refractive index profiles for the multimode fibers
abstract: Consider bell-shaped functions as potentially new refractive index profiles of the fiber with low differential mode group delay. The Fermi-Dirac distribution and Cycloid functions are shown to provide twice or more the fiber-optic bandwidth compared to the conventional quasi-parabolic GRIN. The effect of refractive index fluctuations on the performance of these profiles is analyzed.

articleTitle: All-fiber chirped-pulse amplification system generating 50 MW peak power 400 fs pulses at 1026 nm
abstract: We demonstrate an all-fiber chirped-pulse amplification system. In a stretching stage a specially designed triple-cladding fiber matching with a grating pair compressor allowed to stretch 6 ps 1026 nm pulses from master oscillator to ~500 ps was used. These pulses were amplified in a newly-developed extra-highly-Yb-doped large-mode area fiber up to ~10 W average power and then compressed in a transmission grating compressor down to 400 fs duration with resulted in a record-high 50 MW peak power.

articleTitle: Investigation of the dependence of the dispersion properties of an optical fiber on temperature changes
abstract: the results of studies of the change in chromatic dispersion with temperature, carried out on the developed setup for measuring the differential group delay of signals in an optical fiber at various wavelengths.

articleTitle: Efficiency of 8 µm - emitting quantum cascade lasers with various upper cladding compositions
abstract: We study 8 µm -emitting quantum-cascade lasers with different compositions of upper cladding. The maximum room-temperature peak power exceeds 14W, which is the highest reported value at this wavelength to the best of our knowledge.

Author Keywords: metal organic chemical vapor deposition epitaxy

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of a double arms pump impact in the fiber optical parametric oscillator
abstract: Numerical simulation of a fiber optical parametric oscillator with double arms pump was performed in a wide range of parameters. The use of double arms with photonic-crystal fiber and synchronous pump leads to an increase in the energy of parametric pulses and, when pumps aimed at various points of phase synchronism, to generate pulses previously unavailable in conventional scheme.

articleTitle: Kerr Squeezing in Optical Fibers for Sensitivity Enhancement of Interferometers
abstract: We developed a new simple all-fiber setup for generation of polarization-squeezed states. The setup reliably generates −5 ± 0.5 dB of squeezing which is stable for a long time without any adjustments. We applied this polarization squeezed light to a polarization interferometer and demonstrated an increase of the signal-to-noise ratio by 4 ± 0.5 dB.

articleTitle: Orbital Poincaré solid-state lasers
abstract: We review the direct generation of helical structured light beams, that is orbital Poincare modes including Laguerre-Gaussian and Hermite-Laguerre-Gaussian modes, from laser resonators, and we also address our current research project concerning ultra-compact diode-pumped, optical Poincare Pr: Ylflaser sources, enabling the selective generation of all helical structured light beams mapped on the orbital Poincare sphere.

articleTitle: Cladding-pumped bismuth-doped fiber laser with brightness enhancement
abstract: We present results on the bismuth-doped fiber laser that acts not only as a wavelength converter, but also as a brightness converter. The output characteristics of a Bi-doped fiber laser cladding-pumped by multimode laser diodes at a wavelength of 808 nm were investigated.

articleTitle: Direct Laser Writing of Bragg Gratings in Silica Glass by Helical Motion of a Lenticular Beam Waist
abstract: High quality uniform Bragg gratings of the third order have been inscribed in a single-mode silica-based fiber by a helical motion of a lenticular beam waist of the femtosecond laser. The technique developed paves the way for fabrication of helical fiber Bragg gratings able to change the orbital angular momentum of light.

articleTitle: Interaction of powerful repetition rate femtosecond laser pulses with selfproducted copper nanostructures
abstract: This report is focused on the opportunities of using high energy femtosecond laser radiation for metal nano-structuring and subsequent effective X-ray emission from self-produced nano-structures. We consider the interaction of high energy high repetition rate femtosecond laser pulses from Coherent Astrella Ultrafast Ti:Sapphire Amplifier with shaped copper targets and effective generation of X-ray radiation.

articleTitle: Investigation of a combined absorption-fluorescence-Raman spectroscopy approach to brain tumor tissue differentiation ex vivo
abstract: In this work, we used a combined absorption-fluorescence-Raman approach to the optical investigation of brain tissue. The proposed approach allowed taking into account the blood fill, oxygenation, accumulation of fluorescent biomarker, and Raman signal to estimate a degree of malignancy of the tissue.

articleTitle: Study of the effect of laser pulse duration in the ultraviolet spectral range on fibroblasts
abstract: We report the different pulse duration of UVB laser radiation cytotoxic effect on human skin fibroblasts. The shorter the pulse, the less viable the cells. According to MTT test examined 24 hours after irradiation cells have the potential to recover. Regarding flow cytometry, we concluded that the toxicity is concerned with the lipid membrane destruction.
